papers.title: Model-Uncertainty-Aware Digital Twins for Non-Markovian Quantum Repeater Memories
papers.abstract: Quantum-repeater controllers need reliable estimates of stored entanglement as adjacent links are generated. Fixed exponential lifetimes miss non-Markovian revivals, while complex surrogates are unnecessary when the microscopic family is known. We present QMemTwin, a physics-constrained digital twin that accounts for model uncertainty. It calibrates a bank of contractive passive state-space models, combines their amplitudes with finite-sample-corrected Akaike weights, and abstains when temporal-holdout data indicate unsupported dynamics. Passivity guarantees a completely positive, trace-preserving amplitude-damping channel for each candidate and their convex amplitude average. We evaluate [N cases] synthetic memories: [N supported] supported passive time-invariant cases and [N structural] nonstationary structural-shift cases. In the matched one-pseudomode regime, the correctly specified one-pseudomode fit performs best. Across [N unknown] supported cases with uncertain families, QMemTwin reduces population RMSE by [population reduction]% and Bell-fidelity RMSE by [Bell reduction]% relative to the two-pseudomode model; both paired effects remain significant after Holm correction. The flexible passive model has a slightly lower mean error for unknown families but is statistically indistinguishable from QMemTwin and loses accuracy in the matched regime. The temporal-holdout gate detects [detection]% of structural shifts, with [false alarm]% false alarms on supported families and AUROC [AUC]. In 2-, 4-, and 8-link repeater chains, the mixed cohort shows no significant 8-link goodput gain. A predeclared high-backflow stress cohort yields an 8-link goodput gain of [goodput gain]% over the two-pseudomode model, with paired p = [p value]. These results favor using a known family when available, accounting for model uncertainty otherwise and abstaining on unsupported dynamics.

papers.title: QQLink: A Declarative Framework for Multi-QPU Quantum Workflow Orchestration
papers.abstract: Distributed quantum protocols require measurement outcomes produced at one node to control operations at another. We present QQLink, a programming and orchestration layer that expresses these dependencies in a single program, using workflow nodes, deferred measurement references, and declared entanglement, and derives the cross-node coordination automatically. Its planner constructs a provably acyclic dependency graph in time linear in the total size of the instructions' qubit footprints. The same programs execute through simulator backends or are lowered to dynamic circuits on partitioned quantum hardware. We evaluate seven protocol workflows. Exhaustive feedforward-branch tests on the simulator runtime path, over tomographically complete input sets, yield output-state infidelities of at most $5\times10^{-12}$ and no incorrect classical outputs, and replaying every plan in random topological orders leaves each final state unchanged. Separate executor processes run the plans with delayed messages, with the joint quantum state held by a centralized simulation service. Every run with the full plan is correct, and removing required cross-node dependencies causes protocol failures. The lowered circuits match hand-written implementations of the same construction in two-qubit gate and conditional-block counts. Runs on two IBM Heron processors, each partitioned into virtual QPUs, demonstrate same-chip execution in two sessions a week apart. The runs also show large variation between sessions and losses beyond what calibration-derived noise models predict. Coherence-sensitive checks do not establish coherent Toffoli operation or preservation of the intended repetition-code superposition. These results support QQLink's workflow semantics on the tested execution paths and identify limits of the current hardware realization; execution across physically networked QPUs remains future work.

papers.title: Pauli-ball discrepancy and stability of quantum codes
papers.abstract: The Pauli-ball discrepancy, a quadratic discrepancy summed over all error radii, measures how uniformly the Pauli error images of a $K$-dimensional quantum code cover the $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. At parameters attaining equality in the quantum Singleton bound with minimum code distance $\geq3$, or in the one-error Hamming bound with prime-power local dimension, the discrepancy of every projector of the prescribed rank equals an explicit benchmark plus an exact nonnegative remainder, which vanishes precisely for pure quantum maximum-distance-separable codes and nondegenerate perfect codes, respectively. For a Pauli ball of radius $e$ below half the target distance and size $V_e$, this remainder linearly bounds the squared Hilbert--Schmidt distance of the error-image Gram matrix from the identity. When $KV_e\leq d$, it linearly bounds the diamond error and entanglement infidelity of a noise-independent polar recovery under any noise in that ball's span. For five qubits, we obtain the sharp rank-two Gram constant and exact logical channels of rotated codes attaining this linear order in diamond error. For pure states, the discrepancy equals a pure-state benchmark plus a positive weighted sum of marginal-purity defects, so absolutely maximally entangled states, when they exist, are exactly the minimizers.

papers.title: Two-qubit binegativity can increase under local amplitude damping
papers.abstract: It has been conjectured that the binegativity of two-qubit states is an entanglement monotone. We present a full-rank state as a counterexample: applying amplitude damping to only one of the qubits can increase the binegativity of the state. The output state remains full rank, and the amount of increase can be calculated exactly. In addition, we construct a family of counterexamples that vary continuously with a parameter. In the corresponding one-way local operations and classical communication protocol, the probability-weighted average of the binegativity over the branches after the local measurement is also higher than that of the initial state.

papers.title: Initial-State Preparation for Strongly Correlated Molecules from Matrix Product States: Benchmarking and Environment-Aware Divide-and-Conquer Compilation
papers.abstract: Compiling classically optimized matrix product states (MPSs) into quantum circuits is a promising route to initial-state preparation for strongly correlated molecules, but the accuracy, gate cost, and classical scalability of existing MPS compilation methods have not been systematically assessed. Here, we benchmark representative analytical, variational, and hybrid MPS compilation methods for strongly correlated systems including hydrogen chains and iron-sulfur clusters. We compare state infidelity, CNOT gate count, classical runtime, and parallel scalability across different system sizes and bond dimensions. We also introduce a divide-and-conquer environment-aware compilation algorithm (DCE), which optimizes each local isometry approximation according to its contribution to the prepared-state fidelity. The results reveal complementary operating regimes: direct variational compilation methods are gate-efficient for some smaller molecular systems with $O(10)$ qubits and $O(10)$ bond dimensions or moderate accuracy targets with infidelity of order $10^{-1}$, whereas divide-and-conquer methods scale more favorably for larger systems and relatively higher bond dimensions of $O(10\text{-}10^2)$, particularly when target infidelities below $10^{-1}$ are required. Within the latter family, environment-aware optimization improves accuracy over unitary-distance-based compilation while retaining task-level parallelism. For the FeMo-cofactor (FeMoco), we find the DCE algorithm together with the MPS obtained in the entanglement-minimized orbitals (EMOs) provides a resource-efficient route to initial-state preparation. Our results provide practical guidance for selecting and developing MPS compilation methods for strongly correlated molecular simulations.

papers.title: The Coherent State Projection Eigenvalue Theorem
papers.abstract: Recent papers have developed a cyclic symmetry projected extension for coherent state representations of bosonic Hilbert space. This extension can greatly reduce sampling errors in phase-space simulations of bosonic quantum systems that have symmetries. Here we prove an eigenvalue theorem for the continuum limit of the projected coherent states. Our intuitively appealing result is that in the continuum limit the projected coherent states are eigenstates of the symmetry generating operator. This result gives a differential identity in phase-space that includes the conserved eigenvalues. Detailed applications of these differential identities to obtaining improved Fokker-Planck and stochastic equations in many-body physics will be given elsewhere.

papers.title: Krylov geometry and optimal recovery under uncertain coherent noise
papers.abstract: Recovery from a coherent rotation with an unobserved angle depends on both the encoding and what calibration reveals about the noise. We determine their combined limit for a known finite-dimensional generator and one final recovery. Two polynomial projections organize the answer. A physical Krylov chain separates correctable error amplitudes from their first state-dependent distortion; projection onto lower-angle powers identifies the part that a coherent decoder can cancel. Under explicit rank and moment conditions, their combination gives the exact leading optimal entanglement infidelity at weak noise and a recovery attaining it for any finite logical dimension. The optimal worst-input error lies between one and $d$ times that infidelity at leading order, for logical dimension $d$. When the angle distribution is unknown, we optimize one decoder for every distribution compatible with the calibration. When spectral and calibration frequencies are integer multiples of a common frequency, moment positivity turns this into an exact finite optimization. Small measured means can still allow rare finite rotations. If the sole calibration datum is $β_r=\mathbb E[\sin^{2r}(θ/2)]$, with $θ$ the wrapped rotation phase at that common frequency, the optimal worst-prior infidelity is $O(β_r)$ exactly when generator powers through degree $r-1$ are correctable. When the first uncorrectable power has degree $m<r$, the optimal loss scales as $β_r^{m/r}$, with a sharp coefficient fixed by a universal moment problem. In a loss-free four-photon memory, population measurements at two calibration durations retain the fully informed quartic error coefficient for a fixed symmetric narrow-noise family with positive variance and finite fourth moment; a single duration permits loss quadratic in the noise width.

papers.title: Exact operator bounds on Leggett-Garg violations
papers.abstract: Leggett-Garg (LG) inequalities test whether correlations measured at different times admit a positive joint probability distribution over histories. A violation requires negative values in any joint quasiprobability distribution reproducing those correlations, but such distributions can have negative values even without a violation. Spacetime density kernels extend the density-matrix description to multiple times and are used to study timelike entanglement. We establish a universal bound that relates LG violations to their negative eigenvalue weight. For LG tests involving any number of measurements, we determine the least compatible kernel negativity through an exact relation valid for any system dimension, initial state, dynamics, or measurement rule. This minimum is nonzero if and only if at least one LG inequality is violated. Three-time Lüders LG tests certify at most one eighth of negativity, whereas measurements resolving individual spin levels can approach one half. Including additional incompatible qubit observables gives a further exact minimum that can exceed the LG-only ceiling without increasing the LG violation.

papers.title: Controlling transport with structured long-range hopping
papers.abstract: The combined effects of disorder and long-range hopping play an important role in determining localization and transport in low-dimensional quantum systems. We study transport in a one-dimensional disordered chain with nearest-neighbor hopping supplemented by a long-range hopping term. The long-range coupling is characterized by site-dependent amplitudes that may be either uniform or random. We investigate the interplay between diagonal disorder and long-range hopping, characterizing the resulting transport efficiency. We find that nearest-neighbor hopping in the presence of uniform long-range hopping amplitudes strongly suppresses delocalization over a range of weak disorder. The disorder-enhanced transport regime, established in previous studies, can be understood here as the recovery of delocalization from this strongly suppressed regime. An analytical solution in the Anderson eigenstate basis reveals the microscopic origin of this behavior. In particular, we show that the low-disorder regime of strongly suppressed delocalization can be eliminated by introducing randomness into the long-range hopping amplitudes, providing an additional mechanism for enhancing transport and qualitatively changing the response of the system to disorder.

papers.title: Twirled and swirled worlds: a compositional approach
papers.abstract: Twirled and swirled worlds describe generalised probabilistic theories (GPTs) restricted by symmetry-imposed superselection rules. We extend these constructions to a fully compositional setting for finite-dimensional GPTs and compact groups, treating states, effects, and multipartite transformations uniformly as processes. We distinguish system actions from process-space actions. We define actions on a theory as a whole by requiring the corresponding process-space actions to respect sequential and parallel composition. Averaging physical theory actions defines twirling, while averaging nonphysical theory actions defines swirling. We show that invariant subtheories might not satisfy process tomography, and establish conditions under which they do, involving invariant dynamically faithful states or internal classical reference frames. For locally tomographic parent theories, we prove that every theory symmetry admits a representation by linear system actions and that the invariant subtheory satisfies process tomography. An invariant multipartite process space fails local tomography if and only if some bipartition has sides sharing a non-trivial irreducible representation. We characterise when ancillary systems are necessary, which representations they must carry, and when entanglement is required for ancilla-free process tomography. We develop a framework for unifying twirled subtheories and extend incoherent simulations to compact groups. Finally, we recover bilocal classical theory as a twirled subtheory of classical theory and real quantum theory as a swirled subtheory of complex quantum theory, deriving their tomographic properties from their representation structure.

papers.title: Trial-space co-design for quantum simulation on noisy hardware
papers.abstract: Quantum simulations on noisy hardware are often designed as if the machine were ideal, with device limitations considered only after the basis and measurement plan have been chosen. We instead use information about the physical problem and the device at an earlier stage, to decide which states and evolution times should form a compact simulation basis. Because the target problem remains unchanged, the method adapts only the representation used to solve it. Tests on many-body and molecular models show that this approach can reveal useful directions that ordinary time evolution misses, while also exposing an important limitation: some of these directions can become too similar to estimate reliably. Realistic device data further show that hardware response can change the preferred states and evolution times before execution. Across seven acquisition days, a four-qubit experiment shows a median 54\% reduction in projected-energy error from problem-informed time choices relative to uniform sampling under matched hardware conditions. These results provide a proof of principle for simulation-basis design as a practical interface between quantum algorithms and the hardware that executes them.

papers.title: Genuinely multipartite entangled qudits: one rule to link them all
papers.abstract: Links of rings offer an intuitive picture of multipartite entanglement. Cutting one ring can free some of the others, just as losing a particle, i.e. tracing it out, can disentangle some of the remaining ones. This analogy classifies multipartite entanglement according to which groups of particles stay entangled when others are lost, a question at the heart of robust quantum networks. However, pure states realizing a given link class were known only in special cases. Here, we close this gap. Recasting link polynomials as hypergraphs, we give an explicit formula for pure qudit states and prove that, for every link class, their entanglement under any pattern of particle loss matches the link exactly. The same construction also controls genuine multipartite entanglement, determining exactly which of the groups that stay entangled are genuinely multipartite entangled, and all of them can be made so. As a consequence, we prove the conjecture that $m$-resistant pure qudit states, which stay entangled after the loss of any $m$ particles but become fully separable after the loss of $m+1$, exist for any number of particles and any $m$.

papers.title: Fermion Scattering on Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: Resonant scattering links particle interactions to the formation and decay of unstable excitations. We develop a hybrid quantum-computing framework to study these dynamics through fermion--antifermion collisions. Our formulation of $(1+1)$-dimensional Yukawa theory encodes fermions in qubits and the scalar field in qumodes. We identify the operations needed for a photonic implementation and benchmark the dynamics with tensor-network simulations. Near resonance, we resolve the build-up of a localised scalar excitation and the subsequent partial return of energy to the fermions. Enhanced entanglement accompanies this exchange. Time-dependent correlator measurements reproduce the analytically predicted decay rate to a few percent precision, with energy scans exhibiting a resonance peak consistent with packet-averaged Breit--Wigner behaviour. These results establish a concrete scattering benchmark for hybrid quantum computers and demonstrate how local real-time observables can probe particle-resonance dynamics.

papers.title: Exploiting the Weyl-Chamber Structure for Hardware-Aware Quantum Circuit Compression
papers.abstract: Quantum circuit compression based on tensor networks enables long-time simulation of quantum many-body dynamics on near-term hardware. While Riemannian optimization has been successfully employed for this purpose, it typically optimizes over the manifold of generic two-qubit unitaries. Consequently, the resulting gates must still be synthesized into the hardware's native gate set via KAK decomposition, an overhead that partially negates the original compression gain. We show that Riemannian-optimized gates already exhibit a predictable Weyl structure: near-$R_{ZZ}$ for the Ising model and near-fSim for the Heisenberg XXZ model. Building on this insight, we investigate whether parameterized optimization directly over the native gate set can offer a beneficial trade-off between expressivity and circuit efficiency by reducing the circuit's dimensionality. When comparing the two approaches, we find that the small residual Weyl parameters neglected by the latter are essential for high compression of the Ising propagator, whereas for the Heisenberg propagator, the native XXZ structure can be exploited directly to build a more efficient compressed circuit.

papers.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Medical Imaging: A Primer for Radiologists
papers.abstract: Deep learning has transformed radiology, but the computational cost of training and deploying modern models is outpacing what classical hardware can support. Quantum computing has been proposed as one response to this bottleneck: an n-qubit system can represent $2^n$ states simultaneously, although practical speedups require efficient algorithms, data encoding, and measurement strategies rather than superposition alone. This review introduces radiologists to five core quantum concepts, qubits, superposition, entanglement, quantum gates, and quantum circuits, and to the superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic hardware platforms that define the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. We then summarize the quantum machine learning architectures most often applied to medical imaging (quantum support vector machines, quantum neural networks, variational quantum circuits, and quantum convolutional neural networks) and quantum image representations such as the flexible representation of quantum images (FRQI) and the novel enhanced quantum representation (NEQR). Reported applications include brain tumor classification and segmentation on MRI, pneumonia detection on chest radiographs, skin and breast lesion classification, CT and PET reconstruction, and ultrasound denoising. Nearly all published systems are hybrid quantum-classical pipelines evaluated on small, downsampled benchmark datasets or simulators, and clinical deployment is not yet feasible. We conclude with current limitations and translational priorities for radiology.

papers.title: Entangled logical qubits on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: We demonstrate high-fidelity logical qubit operations using \texttt{ibm\_phoenix}, a square-lattice array of 120 coupled superconducting qubits that are capable of fast reset. Using strategies to exclude underperforming components together with noise informed decoding, we routinely produce surface codes at distance-3 and distance-5 with logical error per round below 1\%. We demonstrate entanglement between two logical qubits, where logical Bell-state fidelities above 93\% are observed for entanglement created via lattice surgery. With three logical qubits and lattice surgery, we perform logical teleportation of a range of states and gates, observing fidelities in the range 78\% - 93\%. Using reset to reduce qubit leakage, we show that repeated rounds of stabilizer measurements continue to exhibit improvements in a stability experiment up to $\sim 2\cdot 10^{-7}$ over 170 measurement rounds.

papers.title: Finite Nonsignalling Resources Suffice to Simulate Entangled Qubits
papers.abstract: A longstanding question in Bell nonlocality is whether finite-alphabet nonsignalling resources can reproduce the continuum of measurement correlations of partially entangled qubits. Here we resolve this problem by showing that every fixed pure two-qubit state admits an exact simulation of all local projective-measurement statistics using shared randomness and finitely many Popescu-Rohrlich (PR) boxes, without communication or postselection. The boxes operate in parallel, with a worst-case bound independent of the measurement settings: at most $128\cot^4θ$ calls for the Schmidt state $\cosθ|00\rangle+\sinθ|11\rangle$, $0<θ<π/4$. The key is an exact finite-selection method that reduces input-dependent continuous sampling to a choice from a fixed-length shared random list, implemented through a finite PR-box network. The construction extends to arbitrary mixed two-qubit states and local binary-outcome POVMs. This reveals a fundamental separation between the continuity of quantum measurement correlations and the alphabet size of the resources needed to simulate them, shedding light on the resource-theoretic structure of Bell nonlocality.

papers.title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
papers.abstract: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.

papers.title: Regulating the crystallization of thermally evaporated perovskites for efficient near-infrared light-emitting diodes
papers.abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02036-5Dual-amide additives regulate the crystallization of thermally evaporated perovskites, enabling near-infrared perovkite LEDs with a peak external quantum efficiency of 25.0%, highlighting their potential for scalable pixelated optoelectronics.

papers.title: Graphical Rigidity of Continuous Variable Graph States under Gaussian Local Transformations
papers.abstract: Multimode entangled pure Gaussian states are an essential resource for continuous variable (CV) quantum information processing. Menicucci et al. [2011] have shown how to describe them as graphs with complex adjacency matrices. Among such complex graph states (CGSs), quantum optics experimental setups straightforwardly display correlations described by purely imaginary graph states (iRGSs) whereas theoretical literature favors off-diagonal real graph state (RGS) descriptions, which actually reflect the entanglement structure in the infinite squeezing limit [Gonzalez-Arciniegas et al. 2021]. We study them beyond this ideal case, thus establishing in the finite squeezing regime an equivalence criterion for the generic case of CGSs through a graph propagating set of conditions which either finds a Gaussian Local Unitary (GLU) converting one state to another or gives a proof of impossibility if such a GLU does not exist. In the experimentally relevant case of the conversion between iRGSs and RGSs, the set of conditions results in simple relations between the topologies of the equivalent real and imaginary graphs. Finally, we show that the canonical forms of iRGSs and RGSs imply that the topology of the CV real and imaginary graph states are too rigid to admit any exact qumode local-addition analogue to the qubit complementation or qudit local-addition, thus demonstrating the non-existence of any exact qumode local-addition for these states. We however define an approximate one when the squeezing is strong enough.

papers.title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
papers.abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement. Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory. Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.

papers.abstract: We provide an equitable partition that gives an exact, minimal representation for the graph Cartesian product formed from quantumlike bits that preserves the relevant spectral and topological properties. papers.title: Generation of perfect spatiotemporal acoustic vortices
papers.abstract: Spatiotemporal acoustic vortices provide an intriguing route to encode transverse orbital angular momentum (OAM) in sound, but they have a fundamental constraint: Normally, their size grows with topological charge. This work overcomes that constraint by experimentally realizing perfect spatiotemporal acoustic vortices whose size remains nearly unchanged across different topological charges. The common vortex size also allows distinct OAM states to overlap and interfere on the same ring, producing programmable petal-like pressure patterns. These capabilities could facilitate acoustic multiplexing and detection, and structured-wave sensing and particle manipulation.

papers.title: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of an ensemble of $N$ two-level emitters undergoing collective decay at rate $Γ$ and collective incoherent pumping at rate $R$, confined to the fully symmetric Dicke ladder. Although the population dynamics are confined to a finite set of rate equations, their quantum-trajectory representation involves infinitely many pump-decay histories. We derive an exact finite continued fraction for the Laplace-transformed Dicke-state populations by resumming the infinitely many quantum trajectories generated by competing pump and decay processes. Our construction provides a physically transparent interpretation of the tridiagonal resolvent and extends to arbitrary permutationally symmetric initial states. In the strong- and weak-pumping regimes, we obtain perturbative transient solutions. We also identify exact relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables at balanced pump and decay strengths. Our solution provides a starting point for extending trajectory-based analytical methods to more general driven-dissipative collective systems.

papers.title: Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points
papers.abstract: Central to non-Hermitian sensing is the question of whether exceptional points (EPs) can make weak perturbations easier to detect. We show that despite enhanced spectral response, in finite-dimensional Lindblad systems with a unique stationary state and a nonzero relaxation gap, EPs offer no fundamental advantage in how the observation time required for reliable detection of a weak perturbation scales with the perturbation strength. We nevertheless demonstrate that by selectively choosing perturbations that enhance the quantum Fisher information rate, EPs can shorten the observation time needed to reach a predefined detection accuracy relative to a comparable non-EP reference at the same decay rate. As an illustration, we show using an optomechanical model at an EP that we can detect a weak force through the cavity output at the same reliability in less time than a non-EP reference. Our results establish fundamental limits on perturbation detection at EPs and can guide the design of faster non-Hermitian sensors based on optomechanical resonators, superconducting qubits, and trapped ions.

papers.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincaré inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Ampère equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.

papers.title: Mediated Interactions between Fermi Polarons in the Strongly Interacting Regime
papers.abstract: Mediated interactions between quasiparticles lie at the heart of Landau Fermi-liquid theory, yet their behavior in the strongly correlated regime is not fully understood. Motivated by recent experiments [Nat. Phys. 20, 68--73 (2024)], we investigate mediated interactions between quasiparticles emerging from a Fermi sea---Fermi polarons---using zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo methods. Our main result is that the Landau interaction between polarons remains repulsive in the strongly interacting regime for any coupling strength in the polaronic branch, in contrast to the downward trend observed experimentally near resonance. Deep in the short-range universal regime, our results are insensitive to the microscopic details of the interaction potential, providing robust evidence for the sign of the ground-state induced interaction. In addition, we determine the real-space interaction between static impurities, recovering a Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY)-like behavior at weak coupling and the nonperturbative Born-Oppenheimer result at strong coupling. More broadly, our results establish a microscopic benchmark for how Landau quasiparticle interactions survive beyond the perturbative regime of strongly correlated quantum matter.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity
papers.abstract: We construct two distinct solutions of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation with the same initial vorticity in $\bigcap_{1\le p<\infty}L^p(\mathbb R^2)$. The vorticities are compactly supported in space and have mean zero, so the corresponding velocities have finite energy. The nonuniqueness mechanism is a cascade of transitions in quadrupole dynamics across infinitely many scales.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
papers.abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact Kähler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.

papers.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
papers.abstract: Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete. We analyze norm control in Muon over the entire training trajectory using the \emph{accumulated effective learning rate}, $C_T=\sum_{t<T}η_t/\|W_t\|_F$, where $η_t$ is the nominal learning rate and $η_t/\|W_t\|_F$ is the effective learning rate relative to the weight norm. For bounded update directions, accumulation over any training interval bounds relative weight displacement. We show that vanilla Muon can accumulate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration and helping explain its slower empirical progress, whereas MuonW and MuonH guarantee at least linear accumulation under the stated conditions. Going beyond bounded-norm control, we show that sufficiently slow norm growth guarantees faster accumulation than the logarithmic worst case, opening up less restrictive optimizer designs. Based on this insight, we propose MuonGS, which uses Gram--Schmidt (GS) projection to remove the radial component of each Muon update without fixing the weight norm. With bounded update directions and a constant nominal learning rate, we prove that the weight norm grows at most proportionally to $\sqrt{t}$ after $t$ steps. Consequently, MuonGS guarantees $C_T=Ω(\sqrt{T})$, with accumulation sustained even in later training. Further, for smooth scale-invariant objectives we establish its $O(T^{-1/2})$ stationarity guarantee. In pretraining experiments with 160M- and 400M-parameter dense models as well as a 135M active- and 1B total- parameter MoE model, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons. In particular, for the dense model it achieves an estimated token-equivalent speedup up to about $15\%$ at matched validation loss to MuonH.

papers.title: Applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles: ODEs, PDEs, integer and difference equations
papers.abstract: Mappings contracting perimeters of triangles are Banach contractions whenever every point of the underlying metric space is an accumulation point. Consequently, applying the perimeter-contraction theorem on a complete metric space without isolated points yields an existence result already covered by Banach's fixed point theorem. This observation applies, in particular, to operators associated with differential and integral equations acting on standard nontrivial function spaces, such as spaces of continuous functions $C[a,b]$, Lebesgue spaces $L_p$, and Sobolev spaces $W^{k,p}$, equipped with their usual norm metrics. Thus, applications extending beyond Banach's theorem for the same operator and metric require a complete invariant domain containing some number of isolated points. Such a domain may be a closed subset of a standard function space, despite the absence of isolated points in the ambient space. The main goal of this paper is to illustrate applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles in settings where the associated operators are not Banach contractions. The differential-equation examples admit interpretations as stylized models combining continuous evolution, nonlocal measurement, and quantized feedback. The integer and difference-equation examples illustrate the effects of rounding on equilibria and periodic responses.

papers.title: Algebraic fiberings of right-angled Coxeter groups on bipartite cone graphs
papers.abstract: We study systems of moves and states in the sense of [JNW21] on certain bipartite graphs, and the associated homomorphisms from the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups to $\mathbb Z$. We give examples of right-angled Coxeter groups whose graphs do not satisfy the legal system criterion, but contain finite index right-angled Coxeter subgroups whose graphs admit legal systems. We also provide a family of examples of graphs without legal systems, where no sequence of the considered graph operations yields a graph with a legal system. Moreover, we show that for a bipartite graph and an orbit of non-empty states under the bipartite system of moves, the associated homomorphism from the commutator subgroup of the right-angled Coxeter group to $\mathbb Z$ has finitely generated kernel if and only if the system is legal.

papers.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP I: The shock region
papers.abstract: We investigate the role of asymmetry in the stationary measures of integrable probabilistic models with boundary interactions. This paper is the first in a series of three focusing on the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP). The stationary measure of open ASEP admits a two-layer Gibbs representation in which a correction term, which we call the Bryc polynomial, encodes the dependence on the asymmetry parameter. We give a probabilistic interpretation of the Bryc polynomial in terms of a birth-death-type Markov chain. As an application, we obtain sharp total variation approximations of the stationary measure by Bernoulli product measures in the high- and low-density phases of the shock region. These approximations yield further applications, including moderate deviation estimates for the stationary measure of open ASEP, as well as asymptotic results for the related model of open ASEP with light particles.

papers.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP II: The coexistence line
papers.abstract: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on the coexistence line. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation, together with the probabilistic interpretation, established in the first paper in this series, of the associated Bryc polynomial in terms of an inhomogeneous birth--death chain. Our main result gives a sharp approximation of the stationary measure. Specifically, we identify the shock location as an explicit observable of the particle configuration and obtain optimal bounds on the total variation distance between its law and the uniform measure on the lattice. Conditional on the shock location, we approximate, in total variation distance, the joint law of the occupation variables away from the shock by Bernoulli product measures with different densities to its left and right. These approximations lead to further applications, including fluctuation limits, moderate deviation bounds for the particle density, and limits for correlation functions under the stationary measure.

papers.title: Classical Verification of Quantum Computation Beyond the Polynomial Hierarchy
papers.abstract: It is not known whether a classical polynomial-time verifier can verify arbitrary polynomial-time quantum computations with an efficient quantum honest prover without computational assumptions. We show that, relative to a classical oracle, such verification is possible for a language beyond the polynomial hierarchy that is decided exactly in quantum polynomial time. The protocol is public-coin, with perfect completeness and soundness error at most 1/4. To our knowledge, no language with such a proof system was previously proved to lie outside AM relative to an oracle. For every unbounded polynomial-time computable function, the oracle can be chosen so that the message count and the oracle query counts of the quantum algorithm, verifier, and honest prover are bounded by this function of the input length. The message count is optimal up to a constant factor, since for a suitable oracle every interactive proof system for the language uses at least a constant fraction of the messages of our protocol on infinitely many lengths, with a constant depending on its verifier. The language is a variant of recursive Fourier sampling in which code tables encode secrets that address data tables. The tables are evaluated recursively, and the oracle stores only the leaves. The quantum algorithm recovers every secret exactly, and the verifier checks the prover's secrets recursively against random code entries. The recursion restricts the input in a correlated way, as the same secret fixes the code bits and chooses the free coordinate, so Håstad's switching lemma does not apply. We prove a switching theorem for these restrictions, which may be of independent interest. For instances of sufficient height, no constant-depth circuit of size $2^{\mathrm{poly}(n)}$ changes its output with probability above $2^{-Ω(n)}$ when the answer of a random instance is flipped by changing a single leaf.

papers.title: Approximate Counting for Mixed $p$-Spin Glasses in Weak External Fields via Cluster Expansion
papers.abstract: We give algorithms for approximating the partition function $Z_N$ of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) model and finite mixed Ising $p$-spin models with $p\ge 3$. The algorithms apply at a fixed margin below the second-moment threshold $β_{\mathrm f}$ with homogeneous weak external fields $|h|\leqρ_0N^{-1/4}$, for fixed $ρ_0>0$. For any accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and failure parameter $δ\in(0,1)$, they approximate $\log Z_N$ to additive error $\varepsilon$. The number of exact operations is polynomial jointly in $N$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $δ^{-1}$. The disorder variables have i.i.d symmetric distribution with unit variance. The failure probability is at most $δ$ plus an explicit disorder tail bound. This tail bound tends to zero under a finite fourth moment condition. Our approach builds on the cluster expansions of Aizenman--Lebowitz--Ruelle~\cite{ALR87} and Dey--Wu~\cites{DW23,DW26}. For higher-order mixtures, we retain hypergraphs using few vertices and evaluate their total weight deterministically through local spin averages and inclusion--exclusion. For SK, we impose cutoffs on the number of vertices of degree at least three and on the total number of edges. We estimate the retained sum using randomized color coding~\cite{AYZ95}. A lower tail control based on reverse hypercontractivity~\cite{MOS13} converts the mean-square approximation of the normalized partition function into logarithmic accuracy.

papers.title: Lower- and upper-$C^2$ integrands: a structured class of functions for stochastic nonconvex optimization
papers.abstract: We study nonconvex stochastic functions that admit a structured second-order representation, a generalization of lower- and upper-$C^2$ functions to normal integrands. Similarly to the deterministic case, lower-$C^2$ normal integrands are defined as the pointwise maxima over a compact random index set of functions that are twice-continuously differentiable in the decision variable with an integrable bounded Hessian. Our main result is a local value function characterization of this class of functions, namely, that they satisfy a local sufficient ascent property almost surely. Equivalently, they differ from a convex normal integrand by a random quadratic. The upper-$C^2$ theory follows by a change of sign, and delivers the corresponding lower envelopes, the form in which these integrands appear as second-stage value functions of stochastic programs with compact recourse. We also show that for this class integrability of the function values, of the local Lipschitz moduli, and of the minimum-norm Clarke subgradients are equivalent. We then study smooth integrands, finite lower envelopes, difference-of-convex integrands, Moreau and forward--backward envelopes, compositions with a smooth map, monotone convex compositions, and compact-recourse stochastic programs within these classes of nonconvex stochastic functions. As an application, we show that the optimistic loss of partial-label regression and the variational formulation of the conditional value-at-risk fit within this framework.

papers.title: Localization, cobordism, and twisted $χ_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$
papers.abstract: We use the method of equivariant localization to obtain a recursion for the cobordism-valued one-point psi-class intersections on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$, and hence the cobordism classes $[\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}]$. Restricting to the hyperbolic formal group law, we recover the Poincaré polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ as a special case, and obtain new formulas for Hirzebruch $χ_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ twisted by tautological line bundles.

papers.title: Shape exclusion for diffusion-limited aggregation
papers.abstract: For diffusion-limited aggregation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, we rule out convergence in volume to bounded regions with boundary measure zero. Moreover, the number of boundary edges grows linearly. For Euclidean DLA in dimensions $2$, $3$, $8$, and $24$, we prove an analogous shape exclusion.

papers.title: Diffusive-dispersive traveling waves and kinetic relations. Generic flux with multiple inflection points
papers.abstract: We consider the broad class of scalar hyperbolic conservation laws with generic non-convex fluxes, which may thus have an arbitrary finite number of inflection points. We investigate the properties of classical and nonclassical shock waves realized as traveling-wave limits of a linear diffusive-dispersive regularization and provide a phase-plane classification beyond the case of a single inflection point. Within the speed range of the generalized Maxwell construction, our main result classifies the left outgoing profiles by their limiting equilibria. In an elementary bowtie configuration, we prove the existence of nonclassical shock profiles with arbitrarily many oscillations. For nested configurations, we order the saddle connections on each entry interval, taking account of inaccessible saddles. We show that the number of oscillations present in the non-classical shock depends on the diffusion-dispersion ratio, and tends to infinity along the elementary families of saddle connections as this ratio tends to zero. Our construction is based on a generalization of Maxwell's equal area rule, which provides us with an invariant region in the phase space for the study of diffusive-dispersive traveling waves.

papers.title: Linear-quadratic mean field games with Volterra dynamics
papers.abstract: We study a class of linear-quadratic mean field games in which the state of each agent follows a stochastic Volterra equation of convolution type. The resulting dynamics are non-Markovian and account for memory effects through a completely monotone kernel, while the mean field interaction enters both the drift and diffusion coefficients. Exploiting a Markovian lifting of the Volterra dynamics, which restores the Markov property at the price of moving to an infinite-dimensional state space, we characterize the optimal response of a representative agent for a given population mean through a system of Riccati equations in Banach spaces, thereby obtaining a feedback representation of the optimal control. We then study the consistency condition defining the mean field equilibrium, which reduces to a forward-backward fixed point equation for the equilibrium mean: we prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium on short horizons and, when the control does not act on the diffusion coefficient, on arbitrary horizons under a monotonicity condition on the interaction. Finally, we consider the corresponding finite-player game and establish a quantitative propagation of chaos result. As a consequence, the feedback control of any mean field equilibrium, when implemented by each agent on its own state, yields an $\varepsilon_N$-Nash equilibrium for the $N$-player game, with an explicit rate as the number of agents tends to infinity.

papers.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP III: The fan region
papers.abstract: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) in the fan region with general boundary rates. The stationary height fluctuations in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region are known to have limits involving Brownian excursions or meanders. We establish discrete counterparts of these limits: on intervals away from the boundaries, the joint law of the occupation variables is approximated in total variation distance by particle configurations constructed from lazy simple random walk excursions and meanders. In the high- and low-density phases of the fan region, we establish Bernoulli product approximations with errors that decay exponentially in the distance from the relevant boundary. Our methods combine refined combinatorial estimates for Motzkin paths and the matrix product ansatz in the totally asymmetric case with a Fourier-type decomposition (based on Askey--Wilson polynomials) of the change of measure for general asymmetry. In addition, in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region, we prove moderate deviation estimates for particle counts on arbitrary sets of sites. These estimates rely on a covariance identity for an auxiliary path measure, through which total nonnegativity (of order two) of the matrices yields negative correlations.

papers.title: Stationary measures of the open KPZ equation: A short proof
papers.abstract: In this note, we give a short probabilistic proof of the two-layer Brownian representation of the stationary measure of the open Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters, conjectured by Barraquand and Le Doussal and recently established in full generality by Dunlap, Gu and Rosati. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation of the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) under Liggett's condition, together with our previously established probabilistic interpretation of the associated Bryc polynomials in terms of inhomogeneous birth--death Markov chains. Martingale estimates yield uniform asymptotics for these polynomials under weakly asymmetric scaling. Combined with known convergence results from open ASEP to open KPZ, these estimates recover the stationary height profile of the open KPZ equation as the first marginal of a reweighted pair of Brownian motions.

papers.title: Generic tensor products are not maximal
papers.abstract: We construct tensor products of uniform matroids which are strictly freer than their generic linear tensor products. In particular, the generic tensor product of two copies of $U_{7,9}$ is not maximal. More generally, for every $a,b\ge2$, this holds for $U_{7,a+7}$ and $U_{7,b+7}$. The construction disproves the uniform tensor-product formulation of Mason's conjecture. Its dual is a relaxation of an explicit circuit-hyperplane of a generic birigidity matroid. By the author's representability theorem, the resulting matroids are non-representable over every field. We also obtain full-rank counterexamples to the Jackson--Tanigawa hyperconnectivity conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$.

papers.title: Iwahori Whittaker functions for unramified quasi-split groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected unramified quasi-split reductive group defined over a nonarchimedean local field $F$. This paper concerns the Iwahori Whittaker functions attached to the unramified principal series of $\mathbf{G}(F)$. We introduce Demazure-Whittaker operators and show that in the non-split case they generate a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters that are determined by $\mathbf{G}$. We then connect these operators to the Whittaker functions, establishing formulas for calculating all values for a basis of Iwahori Whittaker functions and giving a new proof of the Casselman-Shalika formula for the spherical Whittaker function. In doing so we build on the work for split groups of Brubaker, Bump and Licata; the new feature here is the appearance of a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters.

papers.title: On $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles on $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are small modifications of a Fano fourfold
papers.abstract: We find necessary conditions for the projectivization of a rank two vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$ to be related to a smooth Fano 4-fold by a small $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial modification (SQM). Furthermore, we fully describe the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$ when $\mathcal{E}$ is stable, with $c_1=-1$, $c_2=2$. In this case, we prove that there exists a flip from $X^+$ to $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$, where $X^+$ is smooth and Fano. We also determine the birational geometry and numerical invariants of $X^+$.

papers.title: Polynomial automorphisms of C^2 with the same equilibrium measure
papers.abstract: We review the following question: when do two polynomial automorphisms of C^2 have the same maximal entropy measure? While the answer has been known for some time when both automorphisms are compositions of Hénon maps, the general case is more delicate. In this (mostly expository) note we explain how recent results in random dynamics give an almost complete solution to the question, and point out a number of related open problems.

papers.title: On Khovanov local equivalence groups
papers.abstract: Inspired by work in Seiberg--Witten and Heegaard Floer homology, Dunfield, Schütz, and the author constructed an abelian "local equivalence group" built from pairs of chain complexes, and a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group to this group that uses the odd Khovanov complex and the Bar-Natan deformation of the even Khovanov complex. Lewark independently gave a related local equivalence group and concordance invariant, using only the Bar-Natan deformation. In this paper, we construct $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^\infty$ subgroups of Lewark's local equivalence group and the kernel of the map from our local equivalence group to Lewark's, as well as $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$ direct summands of Lewark's group and this kernel, invisible to the $s$-invariants. The construction gives at least six $\mathbb{Z}$-valued concordance homomorphisms linearly independent from $s$, $τ$, and Dai--Hom--Stoffregen--Truong's invariants.

papers.title: GNBG-C: A Unified and Configurable Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization
papers.abstract: Many real-world optimization tasks are governed not only by what should be optimized, but also by what is allowed: a solution must first satisfy physical, operational, safety, budgetary, or structural requirements before its objective value becomes meaningful. Yet benchmark design for constrained continuous optimization often treats these restrictions as fixed properties of predefined test instances. Existing generators and benchmark suites provide essential foundations for reproducible comparison, but they either focus primarily on configurable objective landscapes or expose constraint properties within limited, predefined regimes, making it difficult to ask targeted questions about constraint-induced difficulty: whether an optimizer struggles because feasible regions are small, boundaries are restrictive, variables are tightly coupled, or constraint information is poorly scaled. We introduce GNBG-C, a Generalized Numerical Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization. The central idea is to treat the feasible region itself as a configurable object rather than as an inseparable attachment to a fixed test function. By generating controlled constraint regimes around the known GNBG global minimizer, the generator enables systematic studies in which feasibility pressure can be varied while preserving that point as a global minimizer of the constrained problem. This allows researchers to examine how optimizers discover feasibility, handle constraint pressure, and improve objective quality under diverse and controllable feasibility conditions. GNBG-C therefore provides a flexible and auditable framework for probing the strengths and weaknesses of constrained continuous optimizers under targeted forms of feasibility-side difficulty.

papers.title: Every route counts, but some count more: a max-plus view of the C. elegans brain
papers.abstract: Brains do not simply add up every signal they receive: they select which routes dominate. Yet connectomes are usually analyzed with tools that sum over all paths and place neural states in Euclidean spaces, blurring the feedback circuits that may sustain internal states. Here we treat neural signaling as routing instead of diffusion and describe it with max-plus algebra, in which signals accumulate along a path and the strongest route prevails. We propose a model in which the functional connectome of Caenorhabditis elegans emerges from the time-varying combination of electrical, synaptic, monoaminergic, neuropeptidergic and hormonal layers, and analyze five networks within this framework. Each collapses onto a handful of dominant feedback loops, which recover well-characterized circuits and point to new candidates for experimental study. Unlike linear spectra, these structures keep the biological meaning of the data, and their order-based description suggests that brain states live in lattices rather than Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: A cubic chromatic bound for capped graphs
papers.abstract: An ordered graph is capped if, for any four vertices $a<b<c<d$, the edges $ac$ and $bd$ imply the edge $ad$. We prove that every nonempty capped graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G)\leq\min\{3^{ω(G)-1},18ω(G)^3\}$, where $χ(G)$ and $ω(G)$ are its chromatic number and clique number. This proves a conjecture of Davies, Krawczyk, McCarty and Walczak.

papers.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting. The crucial components of the proof are a long-time Egorov's theorem designed for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle of Cohen--Dyatlov [arXiv:2609.30261], and an application of Weyl's method for exponential sums.

papers.title: Vanishing theorems for $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups of projective Hartogs triangles
papers.abstract: In this note, using J.-P. Demailly's $L^2$ existence theorem for possibly incomplete Kähler metrics, we establish $L^2$ estimates and vanishing theorems for a class of domains in $\mathbb P^n$ without any boundary regularity assumptions. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to M.-C. Shaw's question concerning the vanishing of the $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups of projective Hartogs triangles.

papers.title: No closed-form formula for Stiefel geodesics
papers.abstract: We use differential Galois theory to prove that given two arbitrary points $X$ and $Y$ on the Stiefel manifold, there is no closed-form analytic expression for the Riemannian logarithm $\log_X Y$, the geodesic between $X$ and $Y$, or the geodesic distance between $X$ and $Y$. In other words, these cannot be expressed in terms of elementary functions of the coordinates of $X$ and $Y$; in fact, our result goes further --- even if we allow for repeated integrals of elementary functions, there is still no such expression.

papers.title: Boundary Plateau Laws II
papers.abstract: Given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we classify $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$. The main idea of this paper is due to an LLM, and the paper was written by an LLM, under the guidance of the authors.

papers.title: Boundary Plateau Laws I
papers.abstract: We give a complete list of the possible local shapes of soap films where they wet the whole wire. In rigorous terms, given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we study $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$.

papers.title: Weak tracial approximation and a weak Rokhlin property for C*-dynamical systems
papers.abstract: We extend results on tracial approximability of crossed products from the setting of topological dynamical systems to C*-dynamical systems. For actions of discrete amenable groups on unital C*-algebras, we introduce a weak Rokhlin property which leads to a weak tracial approximation of the crossed products by means of finite direct sums of matrix algebras over hereditary subalgebras of the original algebra. Examples are given.

papers.title: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the $[\mathrm{CNOT}]$ Class with Fibonacci Anyons
papers.abstract: Compilation of two-qubit Fibonacci anyon gates is complicated by leakage ($\ell$) from the four-dimensional computational sector to the fifth state of the fusion space. We construct a GPU pipeline to find low-leakage representatives of the $[\text{CNOT}]$ class on different subsets of the braid group. We exhaustively explore the full positive five-generator alphabet up to $L=21$ with minimal leakage $\ell\sim10^{-3}$ and error $d_{[\text{CNOT}]}\sim 10^{-8}$ on it. To reach larger lengths, the search space is successively narrowed to three-generator, boundary-$σ_3$, and palindromic braids, and by considering only the Garside left normal form. These optimizations allow us to reach $L=72$. For $L=69$, a braid with $\ell\sim10^{-10}$ and $d_{[\text{CNOT}]}\sim 10^{-10}$ is found. In addition to directly enumerating optimal braids, we proved that $\ell\in\mathbb Z[\varphi]$, and any nonzero leakage obeys an exponential lower bound in the braid length, and obtained the limit laws $F_{3,\infty}(\ell)=\ell^2$ and $F_{5,\infty}(\ell)=\ell^4$ for our sets. Using asymptotics for the distribution function $F$, we showed that for sufficiently long braids, the asymptotics of exhaustive search are better than the asymptotics of random sampling for finding low-leakage braids.

papers.title: Systolic pants decompositions with polynomial growth
papers.abstract: We investigate improved bounds on the kissing number of a hyperbolic surface under the assumption that the systole set contains pants decompositions with volume growth constraints. Namely, when the dual graph of the pants decomposition has polynomial volume growth, we obtain a power-savings improvement for the upper bound on the kissing number in terms of systolic length. We also construct super-exponentially many (in $g$) pants decompositions with exponential volume growth for which our techniques still imply stronger upper bounds for kissing numbers. The proofs use the technology of ``stem systems'' and ``tulips'' developed by the first and second author to study $1$-systems of curves.

papers.title: Nonlinear uncertainty principle
papers.abstract: We prove an uncertainty principle for subsets of $\mathbb R$ under weak branching assumptions. We impose a nonlinearity condition on the phase; without it our uncertainty principle fails e.g. for arithmetic progressions. The key ingredient in the proof is Shmerkin's nonlinear projection theorem. This paper is a part of a work in progress, but it is released earlier than the rest of that paper since it is also used in a paper of Cohen-Li-Tao. It also has an overlap with our recent paper [arXiv:2609.30261]; see the end of the introduction for more details.

papers.title: Essential norms of fractional Volterra-type operators
papers.abstract: Given a radial doubling weight $μ$ on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \hat{f}(n)z^n\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, the fractional derivative of $f$ induced by $μ$ is $$ D^μ(f)(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\hat{f}(n)}{μ_{2n+1}}z^n, $$ where $μ_{2n+1}=\int_0^1 r^{2n+1}μ(r)\,dr$ are the odd moments of $μ$. The fractional integral of $f$ induced by $μ$ is $I^μ(f)(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty μ_{2n+1}\hat{f}(n)z^n$. We study the fractional Volterra-type operator $$ V_{μ,g}(f)(z)=I^μ(f\cdot D^μ(g))(z),\quad f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D}), $$ with symbol $g\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, introduced by Bellavita, Moreno, Nikolaidis and Peláez. First, we estimate the essential norm of $V_{μ,g}$ acting on $H^p$ and $A^p_α$. Later, we study the same questions for $V_{μ,g}:H^p\to H^q$ and $V_{μ,g}:A^p_α\to A^q_α$, characterizing their boundedness and compactness and estimating their essential norms for all $0<p,q<\infty$.

papers.title: The packing and covering number of trees are local
papers.abstract: For a graph, its $r$-packing number is the size of the largest $r$-separated set and its $r$-covering number is the size of the smallest $r$-net. We show that the $r$-covering number and $r$-packing number are continuous in the fringe topology on locally finite trees. This recovers convergence results by Meir and Moon for e.g. uniform binary trees, uniform plane trees, uniform Polyá trees and random recursive trees, and proves new results for many other tree models, such as size-conditioned Bienaymé trees, simply generated trees, $m$-ary search trees, the minimum spanning tree of the complete graph and preferential attachment trees. Moreover, our formulation provides an intuitive interpretation of the limiting constant, that also provides an easy route for explicit computations in the case of size-conditioned Bienaymé trees. Our method relies on the definition of a canonical minimum $r$-net, and a relation between covering numbers and packing numbers due to Meir and Moon.

papers.title: Local regularity for solutions to singular and degenerate quasilinear parabolic equations
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to prove local Hölder continuity for weak solutions to quasilinear parabolic equations of $p$-Laplace type under finite integrability assumptions on the forcing, covering the supercritical singular range and the entire degenerate regime. The key ingredient is an $L^\infty$-valued temporal Hölder estimate of the solution after any fixed positive waiting time, which is achieved by coupling a time-rescaling argument with De Giorgi iteration. We also provide counterexamples involving forcing terms with weaker spatial integrability to show that even bounded continuous solutions with compatible data may possess no positive temporal Hölder exponent. In particular, these examples establish the sharpness of the spatial integrability threshold in the degenerate case. Finally, a separate counterexample is constructed to demonstrate that the temporal Lipschitz endpoint can fail for bounded continuous forcing when it depends on time.

papers.title: Constructing Data-Driven Budgeted Uncertainty Sets for Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: In robust optimization, budgeted uncertainty sets offer a popular trade-off between modeling flexibility and computational tractability. Data that is observed in practice is often discrete in nature, which creates the need for tools to construct budgeted uncertainty sets based on observed data. This paper presents a principled approach for this purpose, which ensures that any solution found through the robust problem with respect to the constructed budgeted uncertainty set offers an approximation guarantee with respect to the optimal value of the problem with discrete data. Our approach is purely based on the geometry of data and can be applied to any nominal optimization problem. We discuss the problem of evaluating budgeted uncertainty sets, and how to construct them using exact and heuristic methods. In computational experiments, we show that it is possible to construct sets with little computation time that offer guarantees that are close to optimality.

papers.title: Relative distality and incidence bounds in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We prove Szemerédi-Trotter-type incidence bounds for algebraic relations in any field $F$ admitting a valuation with finite residue field. This includes $\mathbb F_q(t)$, $\mathbb F_q((t))$, and all finitely generated extensions of finite fields. Bays and Martin show that any algebraic $K_{d,s}$-free relation $E\subseteq F^k\times F^\ell$ admits a power-saving in the classical Zarankiewicz bound of Kővári, Sós, and Turán. Answering a question of the authors, we show that this power-saving is uniform in $F$: There is some $ε>0$ depending only on $d$ and the complexity of $E$ (and not on $F$) such that for $A\subseteq F^k$ and $B\subseteq F^\ell$, the number of edges $|E(A,B)|$ is at most $O(|A|^{1-ε}|B|^{1-\frac{1-ε}{d}}+|A|+|B|)$. For the case where $A$ is a set of points and $B$ is a set of lines in $F^2$ and $E$ is the incidence relation, we prove the explicit bound $O(|P|^{\frac{8}{9}}|L|^{\frac{5}{9}}+|P|+|L|)$. As the central ingredient of the proof, we introduce the model-theoretic notion of distality relative to a definable set. We begin developing this notion and prove that the theory of algebraically closed valued fields is distal relative to the residue field. An application of a result of Chernikov, Peterzil, and Starchenko, based on work of Chernikov, Galvin, and Starchenko, yields our incidence bounds.

papers.title: Global Hölder solvability for parabolic equations with interior Morrey data
papers.abstract: We prove global Hölder solvability for uniformly parabolic divergence-form equations with locally finite measure data under an interior Morrey growth condition and a capacity density condition on the spatial domain. The parabolic distance to the initial and lateral boundary is assumed bounded on the source support. For nonnegative data, we establish necessity results that demonstrate the sharpness of the growth and domain assumptions. We also derive estimates for divergence forcing, prove solvability for equations with lower-order terms, and obtain convergence rates in periodic homogenization.

papers.title: Fisher Completions and Statistical Regularization of Wrapped Gaussian Families
papers.abstract: We determine the intrinsic Fisher completion of the full-covariance wrapped Gaussian family on a fixed torus and relate its geometry to uniform estimation. The completion is homeomorphic to the total-variation closure. Every added law is, in suitable integer torus coordinates, a product of a uniform law and a lower-dimensional wrapped Gaussian. All these densities are positive and real analytic, but in dimension at least two no added point has a compact neighborhood. Small balls remain contractible, and explicit minimizing geodesics pass through added points. In dimension at least two, every fixed Fisher neighborhood of an added point has a positive minimax risk at every sample size. For subfamilies with a common positive lower bound on the variance in every nonzero integer direction, we prove that compactness of the completed closure is equivalent to uniform consistency in either $L^1$ or completed-Fisher loss. Equivalently, the Fourier moments must decay uniformly over the subfamily. A fixed covariance floor guarantees this condition without an upper covariance bound and gives $L^1$ risk at most $C_{\varepsilon,d}n^{-1/2}\{\log(n+1)\}^{d/4}$. A common-phase example illustrates how partially uniform limits can retain relative-phase information while remaining uniformly estimable.

papers.title: Approaching Optimal Scaling of Queue Size for an Input-Queued Switch
papers.abstract: We study the scaling of the expected total queue length in an $n\times n$ input-queued switch. It has been conjectured that the optimal scaling is $O(n/(1-ρ))$, up to logarithmic factors, where $ρ$ is the system load. This conjecture has been established in the traditional heavy-traffic regime and in certain sub-regimes of the large-system regime. But it remains unresolved over a wide range of load scalings in the large-system regime. In this paper, we develop a family of scheduling policies parameterized by a positive integer $k\ge 2$. We show that under uniform traffic, our policy achieves an expected total queue length of $O\bigl({n\log\max\{n,1/(1-ρ)\}}\big/{(1-ρ)^{2^k/(2^k-1)}}\bigr)$, as long as $ρ\to 1$ in the large-system regime. As $k$ increases, the exponent $2^k/(2^k-1)$ approaches $1$, bringing our bound arbitrarily close to the conjectured scaling. The expected amortized scheduling cost of the policy is $O(n^3 k)$ per time slot. Our policy is of a batching type, with a novel recursive design that allows an arbitrary number of batching levels. This design principle may also be useful for other scheduling problems in which combinatorial constraints restrict which jobs can be served simultaneously.

papers.title: Statistical Uniformization of Surfaces by Heat-Kernel Fisher Information
papers.abstract: A Brownian particle observed at time $t$ carries information about where it started. On a closed surface this makes the surface itself a statistical model, whose Fisher information pulls back to a heat-smoothed metric $h_t=2tJ_t$; its volume $V_t$ is a normalized Jeffreys volume, and $\log(V_t/2t)$ is the model-dependent constant in Rissanen's minimum-description-length complexity. We ask whether maximizing this statistical size among metrics of fixed area in a conformal class recovers the uniformizing metric. First, $9(A-2πχt-V_t)/t^2$ converges to the curvature energy $\int K^2\,dA$ (the Calabi energy up to a topological constant), uniformly on classes of bounded geometry; hence, within a fixed-area conformal class of bounded geometry containing the uniformizer, approximate maximizers of $V_t$ converge to the constant-curvature metric (on the sphere, to the round metrics). Second, near every flat torus we prove a sharp finite-scale version: for small perturbations whose oscillations are resolved by the diffusion, $t|k|^2\leθ<τ_*$, the flat-subtracted defect is comparable to $\|Δf\|_2^2$, uniformly in the frequency cutoff and over noncollapsing lattices. The explicit threshold $τ_*=4.408\ldots$ is optimal, and it is exactly the observation time at which the information about one curvature mode is maximal. Third, the flat structure is seen only at an exponential scale: the volume loss of a flat torus measures the ambiguity of winding and is comparable to $t^{-1/2}e^{-\operatorname{sys}^2/(16t)}$, which selects the hexagonal lattice as $t\to0$ but not at all times.

papers.title: Model-based clustering of diffusion processes with constant volatility coefficients using high-frequency data
papers.abstract: This paper considers model-based clustering of diffusion processes using high-frequency data. We formulate a finite mixture model for diffusion processes and develop a clustering method based on their constant diffusion coefficients. Using a quasi-likelihood, we propose estimators of the number of clusters, the diffusion coefficients and the cluster labels, and establish their consistency and the asymptotic normality of the diffusion coefficient estimators under high-frequency asymptotics with the number of observed processes fixed. Simulation studies are conducted to investigate the finite-sample performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
