A particular class of such random variables are those whose factorial moments are products and quotients of falling factorials in $n$; we apply our result in this situation and we discuss specific examples arising from block statistics of $k$-divisible non-crossing partitions and from outdegree statistics of rooted plane trees with $k$-divisible outdegrees.

papers.title: The $e$-expansion of integral form Macdonald polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the expansion of the integral form Macdonald polynomials $J_μ(x;q,t)$ in the elementary symmetric function basis. Motivated by the connection between chromatic symmetric functions and LLT polynomials, we conjecture the $e$-positivity of a normalization of $J_μ(x;q,t)$. We verify the conjecture when $μ$ is either a hook or a two-column partition. In the hook case, we express the $e$-coefficients as weighted sums over compositions. In the two-column case, we derive explicit formulas for the $e$-coefficients.

papers.title: Active Flux and Polygons: why a stabilisation and how to implement boundary conditions
papers.abstract: In a recent paper, the authors developed an Active Flux-type algorithm for polygonal meshes (see \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM}). The main difference between Active Flux methods on polygonal meshes and those on Cartesian or simplex meshes is that the basis functions are not explicitly known. These functions describe the solution using point-value approximations on the polygon boundaries and the average value within the polygons. In \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM}, it was shown that directly transposing the algorithm from simplexes to polygons leads to a mild instability, and a remedy was proposed without a rigorous explanation. In the present paper, we clarify this issue and demonstrate that the solution presented in \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM} is indeed correct. Furthermore, another challenge-the implementation of boundary conditions-was previously solved heuristically. Building on \cite{pampa_dg}, we show how to properly implement these boundary conditions. Finally, the method is illustrated through several examples with hybrid meshes.

papers.title: Quantum ordinal selection with two comparisons
papers.abstract: We study the optimal probability of selecting an object within a prescribed rank threshold using at most two noiseless coherent pairwise comparisons of an unknown strict order. Polynomial degree bounds alone can overestimate the success attainable with two comparisons. We develop a comparison-specific semidefinite model that completely characterizes attainable success. Computer-assisted proofs establish the exact optimum for every rank threshold at seven objects and for minimum selection at eight. For minimum selection, we construct an explicit algorithm family and determine its exact optimum. Bounds for all admissible two-comparison algorithms show that the family's asymptotic success is within 0.016% of the unrestricted optimum. We also prove that this relative gap has a strictly positive limit. The optimal quantum-to-classical success ratio for minimum selection converges to approximately 2.48 under the same two-comparison budget.

papers.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
papers.abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $Δ(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $Δ(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

papers.title: Exceptional times of compact support for $α$-stable superprocesses
papers.abstract: We consider symmetric $α$-stable Dawson--Watanabe superprocesses on $\mathbb R^d$ for every $d\geq1$ and $0<α<2$, started from an arbitrary nonzero finite measure. We prove that, almost surely, the times at which the spatial support is compact and nonempty have Hausdorff dimension one in every nontrivial interval before extinction. We also prove that, almost surely, the times at which the support is contained in any prescribed neighborhood of the extinction point have Hausdorff dimension one in every nontrivial interval ending at extinction. These results extend the corresponding conclusions for $0<α<2/3$ to the full stable range. The key new ingredient is a uniform zero-set theorem of independent interest for Feller branching diffusions started from zero with deterministic continuous cumulative immigration. It shows that sufficiently small total immigration ensures that the zero set on a prescribed open interval has Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to one, with arbitrarily high probability. The estimate is uniform over the immigration profile and allows singular continuous immigration measures.

papers.title: A High-Order Geometric-Compatible DGSEM with Subcell Limiting for the GPR System
papers.abstract: We construct an equation-of-state-independent geometric-compatible finite-volume (GC-FV) method and a high-order nodal discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element extension (GC-DG) for a reduced Godunov-Peshkov-Romenski system on fixed Eulerian meshes. Density is recovered from $ρ=ρ_0\det(\mathbf{A})$, so mass conservation is a hidden companion law of the distortion equation. Starting from a straight-path Dal Maso-LeFloch-Murat fluctuation pair, minimum-change cofactor projections produce a single-valued density flux and exact induced local Lax-Friedrichs dissipation without jump quotients. The summation-by-parts property lifts the geometric two-state identity to high order and yields an equivalent subcell representation of GC-DG. We then blend GC-DG with the compatible GC-FV operator on the same Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto subcells. Because both operators induce the same boundary density flux, the global subcell blend retains the exact semidiscrete mass balance while suppressing shock-generated oscillations. A complementary modal/face-jump indicator supplies the elementwise blending coefficient. Numerical experiments verify high-order convergence, the expected temporal scaling of the fully discrete mass drift, and robust shock capturing for fluid, nonlinear-elastic, thermal-wave, and elastoplastic problems, including genuinely multidimensional configurations.

papers.title: Propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a time-periodic shifting environment
papers.abstract: The current paper is devoted to the study of the propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a shifting environment. We investigate the scenario in which the favorable and unfavorable habitats are spatially separated, with the favorable habitat shifting at a time-periodic speed. We first establish the vanishing, persistence, and spreading properties of solutions with compactly supported and front-like initial data. In particular, we show that if the self-limitation rate of the species is large relative to the chemotactic sensitivity and the species is initially confined to a bounded region, then the species eventually becomes extinct when the habitat shifts rightward with a large average speed. In contrast, when the average shifting speed of the habitat is moderate, the species can persist and spread along the shifting habitat into an increasingly large spatial region. Finally, we establish the existence and nonexistence of time-periodic forced wave solutions whose wave speed coincides with the average shifting speed of the habitat.

papers.title: Linear Hashing Is Poissonesque
papers.abstract: The Poisson approximation theorem states that when $m$ balls are tossed uniformly and randomly into $n$ bins, the distribution of the bin loads can sometimes be approximated by $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. We show that when the balls are tossed via a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map, the load distribution is still governed by this Poisson distribution, albeit in a (necessarily) weaker manner. This allows us to show that a random linear map behaves like a fully random map in the following ways: 1. $\textbf{Expected loads.}$ We show that the expected value of the $r$th largest bin is governed by the $r$th largest value among $n$ independent Poisson random variables of mean $m/n$. Specializing to the canonical setting of $m=n$ and $r=1$, our bounds show that the expected maximum load when $n$ balls are hashed into $n$ bins by a random $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear map is no more than the corresponding expectation for a fully random map $\textit{plus}$ $\frac{3}2 + o(1)$. Specializing to $m\gg n\log n$, we show that the expected max load is $(1+o(1))m/n$ in this regime. 2. $\textbf{Concentration.}$ When $m\gg n\log (1/ρ)$ balls are tossed into $n$ bins randomly, we expect with $0.99$ probability that $\textit{every}$ density-$ρ$ subset of bins will contain a $(1\pm o(1) )ρ$-fraction of the balls. We show that this remains the case if the $m$ balls are tossed using a random linear map, and our bound matches the $o(1)$-factor produced by the fully random case. This gives a stronger version of the Leftover Hash Lemma for linear maps. An implication of this is that all bins have load $m/n \pm O(\sqrt{(m/n)\log n})$ with probability $0.99$. We obtain these results by showing that the average of a log-potential on the bin loads is upper bounded by the cumulant generating function of a Poisson random variable of mean $m/n$.

papers.title: Floer lasagna modules for some 2-handlebodies
papers.abstract: Morrison, Walker and Wedrich used Khovanov homology to define the skein lasagna module for a 4-manifold with a link in its boundary. The skein lasagna module was shown to be a deep and powerful invariant; in particular, Ren and Willis proved that it detects exotic smooth structures. Still, computing the skein lasagna module outside some carefully chosen grading range remains an important open problem. Motivated by this construction, Chen defined the Floer lasagna module using Heegaard Floer link homology. In this paper, we give a complete, but partially conjectural description of Floer lasagna modules for a class of 4-manifolds obtained by adding 2-handles along plumbed L-space knots (with certain framing constraints). In particular, we prove that for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ it is infinite-dimensional, and conjecture that for $\mathbb{CP}^2$ it is infinite-dimensional as well. We compute this module for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ (and conjecturally for $\mathbb{CP}^2$) in all Alexander and Maslov gradings. This strengthens and extends the recent results of McCulloch.

papers.title: Positivity of simplicial volume and uniqueness for the twelve-vertex flag three-spheres
papers.abstract: We study the twelve-vertex flag triangulation $T_{12}$ of $S^3$ and the Davis $4$-manifold $M(T_{12})$ associated with it. We prove that $T_{12}$ is, up to isomorphism, the unique flag triangulation of $S^3$ with twelve vertices in which every edge is contained in a square; this proves Milizia's Conjecture~6.31. We also prove a general criterion for the tangent Euler class of a Davis $4$-manifold to be bounded, and we verify it for $T_{12}$ by means of an explicit symmetric form. Since the Euler class takes the value $256$ on the fundamental class of $M(T_{12})$, the duality between bounded cohomology and simplicial volume gives $\|M(T_{12})\|>0$. This answers Milizia's Question~1.7.

papers.title: Unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in $H^{1/2}(\Bbb T^3)$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) in the scaling-critical class $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$. Unlike approaches based on the GP-hierarchy or normal form reductions, which typically involve higher-order expansions, our proof works directly with the original cubic NLS, where we also make use of several new a priori Euclidean-like Strichartz estimates. More precisely, we show that every distributional solution in $C_tH_x^{1/2}$ belongs a priori to the class $L^2_{t,\mathrm{loc}}L_x^6$. The key ingredients are a suitable high-low modulation decomposition and the compactness of solution trajectories on bounded time intervals. We also exploit the preservation of the canonical symplectic form under the truncated NLS flow, in order to obtain necessary stability estimates in the rough Sobolev space $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$.

papers.title: An isometric embedding of the space of non-increasing sequences with non-negative terms into the Gromov-Hausdorff space
papers.abstract: The Gromov-Hausdorff space is a certain metric space induced by the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence, and we study an isometric embedding into this space. While the subspace of non-negative real numbers in the Euclidean space admits an isometric embedding, we prove that the subspace of $\ell^\infty$ consisting of non-increasing sequences with non-negative terms can be isometrically embedded into the Gromov-Hausdorff space.

papers.title: The_Quadratic_Conjecture_and_p-groups_of_maximal_class
papers.abstract: The Quadratic Conjecture for finite p-groups, which is equivalent to the Strong Oliver Conjecture, asserts that if a finite p-group G acts faithfully on an F-module V, then the center Z(G) contains a quadratic element. In this paper, we investigate the structure of maximal class p-groups and establish that they satisfy the Quadratic Conjecture.

papers.title: Resolution quivers and the QF-1 property of higher Auslander Nakayama algebras
papers.abstract: We give a resolution-quiver-theoretic proof of the QF-1 conjecture of Cruz and Marczinzik for higher Auslander Nakayama algebras of positive even global dimension. The proof combines syzygy calculations in Kupisch coordinates, which show that the projective dimensions of quotients of a fixed projective module with cyclic top strictly decrease as their lengths increase, with a torsion-pair argument and Morita's criterion.

papers.title: Target Detection with Asymmetric Gaussian Classical Correlation
papers.abstract: We study the characteristics of two-mode classical correlation in Gaussian regime, which is produced by impinging a thermal state into a beam splitter. It is explicitly investigated how a measurement on one mode affects the other. The result enables the distinction between classical and quantum correlations. Then, we show how classically correlated states are advantageous in target detection, specifically for an asymmetric classical correlation with different mean photon numbers in the signal and idler modes. Under on-off detection, the classically correlated states significantly outperform quantum correlated states as the environmental thermal mean photon number increases. Furthermore, we demonstrate the advantage of local Gaussian operations in the target detection.

papers.title: Rank-one Factored Gradient Descent without Restricted Isometry: Application to Quantum Pure State Tomography on Multi-Qubits
papers.abstract: Factored gradient descent (FGD) is a scalable nonconvex method for low-rank positive semidefinite matrix recovery, in which the rank and positivity constraints are satisfied automatically by the factorization. Most of the existing theory that certifies benignity of its loss landscape, however, relies on a restricted isometry property (RIP) of the measurement map. In quantum state tomography, one of its applications, the measurements that can be acquired with stable statistics are limited by detection efficiency and drift to Pauli observables of low weight; we first show that under such partial-weight Pauli measurements RIP fails in the worst possible way. We then bundle the mutually commuting observables setting by setting, pushing the state forward to the probability distribution of each setting, and introduce a max-sliced total-variation loss. On the stratum where the setting attaining the maximum is unique there is no spurious local minimum, and provided only that the measurement map is injective on generic pure states, the global minimum is the truth up to a phase. Finally we verify these claims numerically on four qubits and compare against FGD with the ordinary loss.

papers.title: Local Reflexivity and Exactness for Reduced $C^*$-Algebras of Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every countable non-exact discrete group $H$ and every nontrivial countable discrete group $K$, the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is not locally reflexive. These provide the first known examples of non-locally reflexive reduced group $C^*$-algebras, settling a longstanding existence question. Moreover, for every nontrivial countable exact discrete group $K$, we establish that local reflexivity of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is equivalent to exactness of $H$, and hence to exactness of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$. This gives a partial affirmative answer to Kirchberg's question of whether local reflexivity implies exactness for $C^*$-algebras. As applications, we construct finitely generated groups with the Haagerup property, as well as finitely generated residually finite groups, whose reduced group $C^*$-algebras are not locally reflexive. In particular, neither the Haagerup property nor coarse embeddability into Hilbert space guarantees local reflexivity of the associated reduced group $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: An efficient coupled block preconditioner for the Marker-and-Cell discretization of the Stokes-Darcy equations
papers.abstract: We consider the iterative solution of the large, sparse and nonsymmetric double saddle-point systems arising from the stationary Stokes-Darcy equations in two dimensions, discretized by the Marker-and- Cell (MAC) finite difference method. Existing block triangular preconditioners rest on approximations of two Schur complements, the second of which is hard to approximate uniformly in the physical parameters. We propose instead a coupled preconditioner that keeps the interface coupling and regularizes the constraint block by a small multiple of the identity, so that the second Schur complement never has to be approximated. We analyze the spectrum of the preconditioned matrix, both in the ideal case and for the inexact version used in computations, and derive from it a rule for scaling the regularization parameter with the physical parameters. Numerical results show mesh-independent convergence of preconditioned GMRES and robustness with respect to the viscosity and the permeability.

papers.title: Sharp $L^p$--$L^q$ bounds for the strong circular maximal operator
papers.abstract: We study $L^p$--$L^q$ boundedness of the strong circular maximal operator $\M$, the maximal function over axis-parallel ellipses centered at the origin whose two semiaxes range independently over $[1,2]$. We prove that $\M$ is bounded from $L^p$ to $L^q$ whenever $(1/p,1/q)$ lies in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2/7,1/7)$, and $(1/3,1/3)$, the two-parameter analogue of the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2/5,1/5)$, and $(1/2,1/2)$ obtained by Schlag and Schlag--Sogge for the circular maximal function. The range is sharp up to the boundary; in particular, weak type $(p,q)$ bounds fail for every $p\le3$. The proof is based on a bilinear estimate for frequencies in separated angular sectors, uniform as the sectors approach the coordinate axes. We also prove the analogous sharp result for axis dilations of a translated circle $c+\mathbb S^1$ with fixed $c\ne0$, where the vertex $(2/7,1/7)$ is replaced by $(1/4,1/8)$.

papers.title: Isometric Theory for Greedy-Type Properties with Enlarged Greedy Sums
papers.abstract: For a semi-normalized Markushevich basis, we study isometric almost-greedy inequalities in which a greedy sum of $φ(m)$ terms is compared with coordinate projections onto at most $m$ terms. Here $φ$ is any strictly increasing map of the nonnegative integers into themselves with $φ(0)=0$. We sandwich $φ$-almost greediness with constant $1$ ($φ$-AG$_1$) between two levels of symmetry for largest coefficients (SLC): $$φ\mbox{-SLC}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ φ\mbox{-AG}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ \mbox{weak }φ\mbox{-SLC}_1.$$ Both implications are equivalences if and only if $φ(1)\le2$. We then characterize $φ$-AG$_1$ by the weighted weak $φ$-SLC or a single homogeneous norm inequality, called Property $(F_φ)$.

papers.title: Beyond Deduplication: Sharp Retrieval Limits for Attention with Correlated Distractors
papers.abstract: Redundant context affects attention through two distinct mechanisms: repeated items add normalization mass, while score variation within correlated groups can produce extreme individual scores. We separate these effects in a planted retrieval model with exponentially many Gaussian distractors arranged in known, exponentially large clusters. The model is a two-level generalized random energy model, whose classical free energy yields exact retrieval thresholds. Gaussian interpolation further shows that increasing positive correlation at fixed token count lowers the distractor free energy, unlike adding duplicates. Our main result identifies a sharp limitation of subtracting log cluster size from pre-softmax scores: this correction removes multiplicity but retains within-cluster extremes. Even a temperature chosen after observing all scores cannot lower the required signal below $\sqrt{2α_1}$, where $α_1$ is the exponential rate of the number of clusters. Averaging scores before exponentiation instead suppresses these fluctuations and achieves $\sqrt{2ρα_1}$, where $ρ$ is the within-cluster correlation. The gap persists after adding exponentially many singleton distractors, so group size alone does not identify the target, and extends to fixed finite hierarchies of light-tailed independent-increment scores. Finite-sample, stability, and participation results complement the asymptotic analysis. A controlled retrieval experiment with frozen sentence embeddings supports this distinction while delineating its scope: averaging helps when the relevant item is a singleton, but can discard useful evidence when a relevant group contains multiple matching items.

papers.title: Abelian quotients and orbit sizes for subgroups of linear groups
papers.abstract: Keller and Yang formulated two conjectures relating abelian quotients of subgroups of finite linear groups to largest orbit sizes. After counterexamples were found to the original conjectures, two revised versions were proposed. We prove both revised conjectures for every finite group $G$ satisfying $F(G)=F^*(G)$. We also extend a regular-orbit theorem for nilpotent subgroups to completely reducible modules of mixed characteristic under the same hypothesis.

papers.title: Sheaves on nodal singularities I
papers.abstract: We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve $x^uy^v=0$, and the punctual Quot schemes of the module $k[[x]]^u\oplus k[[y]]^v$ over the reduced node $xy=0$. We compute their motivic generating functions for all $u,v$ and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution $\mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L}$. This proves the Hilb--Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb--Quot--HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.

papers.title: A Deterministic Game-Theoretic Approach to Convexity-Preserving Property and Finite-Time Extinction of Level Sets for Geometric Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the convexity-preserving property and finite-time extinction of level sets for quasilinear geometric equations using a game-theoretic approach introduced by Kohn and Serfaty. To construct the game whose value function approximates the viscosity solution, we use the approach introduced by Sato.

papers.title: A Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Biharmonic Dirichlet Control Problems With Patch Reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present and analyze an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for Dirichlet boundary control problems governed by the biharmonic equation, with the control imposed through the normal derivative. The method is based on a reconstructed discontinuous approximation that admits an arbitrarily high-order approximation space with only one unknown per element. We construct a discretization that approximates the state and adjoint state in this space and derive a priori error estimates in the energy and $L^2$ norms. The analysis is carried out under the limited regularity available on polygonal domains by means of a medius argument. Numerical experiments are provided to support the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: Neutrinos as Quantum Information Carriers? A Gap Analysis Against the DiVincenzo Criteria
papers.abstract: Photons, trapped ions, neutral atoms, and superconducting circuits are all well-known quantum information platforms. Neutrinos offer a unique possibility, displaying quantum interference (flavour oscillation) over thousands of kilometres, yet interacting so weakly that they can travel through the Earth with minimal interaction. This short paper is a gap analysis. We use information from the existing literature to compare neutrinos to the seven DiVincenzo requirements. Firstly, there are five requirements to do with computation and secondly two requirements to do with communication. We analyse where the gaps are for each requirement. Overall, we find that neutrinos have high fidelity and good coherence; however, they do not have a clear qubit definition and initialisation. They do not have universal gates, individual qubit readout, or stationary-to-flying conversion, meaning they either fail or are very poor. Therefore, we think they are best considered as an exceptional flying information carrier; however, they are very difficult to control. We have outlined all of the gaps which can be used to inform future work.

papers.title: Chern holonomy under the first and second Chern--Ricci flows
papers.abstract: We compare the Chern holonomy of the first and second Chern-Ricci flows on compact complex manifolds. For the first flow, we construct an explicit immortal pluriclosed solution on a complex two-torus with full and restricted holonomy $U(2)$, except at one finite time when both groups are $U(1)^2$; its smooth limit has holonomy $SU(2)$. The solution is uniformly nondegenerate and has bounds of every fixed differential order for all time. In contrast, the second Chern-Ricci flow preserves full and restricted Chern holonomy under the natural unitary identification, including the initial time and nonclosed groups. The proof combines preservation of a connection reduction, positive-time analyticity, and a path-transport comparison. As an application, the optimal minimum mean curvature on a holomorphic bundle is unchanged when metrics are restricted to any realizable full and restricted holonomy class. An explicit projected-curvature source explains the failure of the corresponding Ricci-flow holonomy argument.

papers.title: A Two-Grid Finite Element Method for the Nonlinear Poisson-Boltzmann Equation Based on a Solution Decomposition
papers.abstract: The nonlinear Poisson--Boltzmann equation (PBE) is a widely used implicit-solvent model for the electrostatics of biomolecules in ionic solvent. Its numerical solution is complicated by the point charges, the dielectric jump across the molecular surface, and the exponential nonlinearity. We study a two-grid finite element method for the PBE built on the solution decomposition $u=G+Ψ+\Phit$ of Xie [J.~Comput.~Phys.~275 (2014) 294--309], in which $G$ carries the singularities analytically, $Ψ$ solves a linear interface problem, and $\Phit$ solves a semilinear interface problem for an arbitrary number of ionic species. The nonlinear problem for $\Phit$ is solved on a coarse mesh only, followed by a single Newton correction on the fine mesh, so that only symmetric positive definite linear systems are solved on the fine mesh. The analysis uses a $C^2$ truncation of the exponential that grows quadratically beyond a level $τ$; for $τ$ above an explicit bound the truncated problem has the same solution as the original one, and no discrete maximum principle or mesh-angle condition is needed. Under standard piecewise regularity assumptions we prove quasi-optimal energy and $L^2$ estimates and an $L^4$ estimate for the finite element approximation of $\Phit$, and for the two-grid solution we prove $\enorm{u-\utg}\le C\big(h^{s-1}+H^{2(s-1)+t/2}\big)$ in three dimensions, where $t=\min\{s,σ\}-1$. Whenever the dual problem is at least as regular as the primal one ($σ\ge s$), the coarse mesh can be chosen as $H\sim h^{2/5}$ without loss of accuracy. A manufactured-solution test confirms the predicted rates and the quadratic dependence of the two-grid correction on the coarse error.

papers.title: Stability functions inducing stability data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study when a stability data on an abelian length category is induced by a stability function. We give an intrinsic characterization of such stability data. For at most six phases, an inducing function exists if and only if every semistable subcategory is wide. An example with seven phases shows that this bound is sharp. For finite phase sets and finite rank, an inducing function exists if and only if an inducing red path exists. We also give a maximal green sequence of length eleven in type $D_4$ that no stability function induces. This disproves the red-path conjecture of Brüstle--Smith--Treffinger.

papers.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp dimensional dependence of the asymptotic approximation error for the Euclidean unit ball $B_2^d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ by polytopes with a prescribed number of vertices in the relative symmetric difference metric. Specifically, we prove that $$\lim_{N\to\infty}N^{2/(d-1)}\inf_{P\in P_d(N)}\frac{\operatorname{vol}_d(P\triangle B_2^d)}{\operatorname{vol}_d(B_2^d)}=Θ(d^{-1/2}),$$ where $P_d(N)$ consists of polytopes with at most $N$ vertices and no containment restriction. Equivalently, the classical Laguerre-Delone triangulation numbers satisfy $\operatorname{ldel}_{d-1}=Θ(d^{-1/2})$. This improves the lower bound $Ω(d^{-1})$ of Böröczky (2000) and the upper bound $O(1)$ of Ludwig, Schütt and Werner (2006). In contrast, the corresponding asymptotic coefficient for approximation with a prescribed number of facets has order one, as shown by Kur (2020). We also establish non-asymptotic bounds showing that, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the ball admits an $\varepsilon$-approximation with at most $\exp(C(\varepsilon)\sqrt d)$ vertices, whereas approximating the hypercube to the same accuracy requires at least $\exp(c(\varepsilon)d)$ vertices. Consequently, the ball does not maximize the optimal relative approximation error among convex bodies, even up to an absolute multiplicative constant at the same vertex budget. Thus Macbeath's theorem (1951) on the extremality of the ball for inscribed approximation does not extend to polytopes in arbitrary position.

papers.title: A simple twist to altermagnetism
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03495-xTwo-dimensional altermagnets hold promise for next-generation spintronics but remain difficult to synthesize. Now, altermagnetism has been observed in an orthogonally twisted van der Waals homostructure, opening possibilities for ultrathin devices.

papers.title: Hodge Theory and Grobner Degenerations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of mixed Hodge structures under square-free Grobner degenerations. We show that the weight-zero part of singular cohomology and the zeroth graded piece of the Hodge filtration are preserved under such degenerations, complementing the homological rigidity established in the seminal work of Conca and Varbaro. We use these results to settle their conjecture concerning the singularities of homogeneous coordinate rings admitting such degenerations.

papers.title: The Inhomogeneous Kinetic FPUT Equation near Rayleigh-Jeans Equilibria
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear dynamics of the spatially inhomogeneous kinetic wave equation associated with the FPUT-$β$ problem. We prove global-in-time well-posedness near nonsingular Rayleigh-Jeans equilibria and their asymptotic stability in particular in weighted $L^\infty$ norms in space and momentum, for small initial perturbations orthogonal to the collision kernel at almost every spatial point. We describe the spectrum near the origin at small spatial frequencies, identifying two simple eigenvalues with fractional and diffusive orders $|ξ|^{8/5}$ and $ξ^2$, respectively. Combining this spectral analysis with energy estimates taking into account the transport effect, we establish algebraic decay for the linear semigroup despite the absence of a spectral gap for the collision operator. We then use these estimates to obtain nonlinear stability.

papers.title: Quantum Anomaly Detection in network traffic using Variational Quantum Classifiers
papers.abstract: The increasingly complex cybersecurity landscape requires more advanced network anomaly detection systems. Although, classical machine learning models are known to be effective, they reach computational bottlenecks when processing high-dimensional data. This study investigates the potential of Quantum Machine Learning (QML) for network traffic anomaly detection by evaluating four distinct Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) architectures. A synthetic network traffic dataset is generated for the evaluations. The VQC models systematically varied feature encoding methods, parameterized ansatz circuits, quantum neural network types, and classical optimizers. Experimental results show that a trade-off exists between circuit expressivity and optimization stability. Deeper circuits (VQC-4) achieved higher accuracy of upto 89.0\%, while simultaneously being sensitive to training conditions. A shallower variant (VQC-1) under performed, although it had consistent and stable optimization curves. Class-dependent biases were also observed such as in VQC-2, where the model struggled to find an effective decision boundary, and produced a large number of false negatives. The best performing model in this study (VQC-3) combined ZFeatureMap with RealAmplitudes ansatz, optimized using ADAM. Comparative analysis against classical machine learning models such as Support Vector Machine and Random Forest reveal a performance gap, where classical models are able to achieve perfect classification performance on the synthetic data. It is concluded that classical algorithms remain dominant in their ability to classify structured data with relatively simple class separations. However, due to the observed potential of certain VQC configurations to learn decision boundaries to classify data, their utility for future applications in noisier, higher-dimensional problems is highlighted.

papers.title: Quantum wedges and large deviations for SLE with two force points
papers.abstract: We prove a good large deviation principle for chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_κ(W_1-2;W_2-2)$ with force points at $0^-$ and $0^+$, for every fixed $W_1,W_2>0$, as $κ\downarrow0$. The topology is Hausdorff convergence of the entire compact trace. The rate has two equivalent descriptions: the sum of the component wedge energies obtained by cutting a deterministic ambient wedge, and the Loewner driving energy relative to the force-point drift.

papers.title: Dynamics-Aware Sampling and Recovery for Tensor-Valued Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We study sampling and recovery for tensor-valued dynamical systems evolving under the t-product, using partial spatial observations over time. Although the t-product Fourier transform yields slicewise matrix dynamics, recovery does not generally decouple across slices. Eigenvalues shared across Fourier-domain frontal slices couple the corresponding eigenspaces into aggregated spectral blocks, which determine the tensor-specific recovery geometry and space--time tradeoff. We establish deterministic identifiability conditions for the initial tensor state. In the diagonalizable case, these are frame conditions on the aggregated blocks. We extend them to non-diagonalizable systems through generalized eigenspaces and Jordan structure. A temporal--spectral factorization of the finite-horizon stacked recovery system underlying Tensor Dynamical Sampling (DS) yields a decoupled two-stage formulation once the temporal threshold is reached. Under independent spatial subsampling, we prove high-probability recovery guarantees using empirical Gram matrices on the aggregated blocks. The bounds depend on aggregated multiplicities, incoherence, and population conditioning. Stability estimates separate the spatial frame factor from the temporal Vandermonde factor and show that increasing temporal depth may worsen numerical conditioning even after identifiability is ensured. We implement Tensor DS and evaluate it on synthetic and real data. Phase transitions track the predicted blockwise sampling thresholds, and stability experiments illustrate Vandermonde conditioning. Experiments on sea surface temperature and turbulence velocity data show that a learned t-product system operator generally yields more accurate and structurally faithful reconstructions than vectorized low-rank, Tucker-type, graph-regularized, graph-spectral, and vectorized dynamical sampling baselines.

papers.title: Higher Order OTOCs in Chaotic Quantum Maps: Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances and Asymptotic Freeness
papers.abstract: Out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) measure the scrambling of information and are a powerful diagnostic of chaos. In chaotic quantum systems with a classical analog, their relaxation towards equilibrium is dictated by the classical Ruelle--Pollicott resonances. We investigate higher-order OTOCs in quantum maps, prototypical one-body systems with a classical limit showing all the essential features of chaotic dynamics. We demonstrate numerically that in the intermediate-time regime they decay exponentially at a rate that depends only on the parity of the order: odd-order OTOCs decay at the same rate as classical correlations, given by the leading Ruelle--Pollicott resonance, and even-order ones at twice that rate. Both are far slower than the naive expectation, under which the rate would grow in proportion to the order. We then mimic the effect of an environment by defining a coarse-grained superoperator whose effect is to introduce decoherence into the system, and find that the expected proportionality between rate and order is thereby restored. Finally, we show that at long times each higher-order OTOC becomes dominated by a single free cumulant, whose saturation value falls off inversely with the dimension of the Hilbert space, signalling the emergence of asymptotic freeness and highlighting the relevance of free probability theory as a framework for the study of quantum chaos.

papers.title: A proof of the Grothendieck join-meet positivity
papers.abstract: We prove the (signed) Grothendieck join--meet positivity $$ G_{λ\veeμ}G_{λ\wedgeμ} -G_λG_μ\in \sum_ν \mathbb{N}\cdot (-1)^{|ν|-|λ|-|μ|}G_ν$$ for stable Grothendieck polynomials using geometric Satake equivalence, thereby resolving a conjecture posed by Thomas and Yong.

papers.title: Finiteness theorems for trace Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields
papers.abstract: Motivated by Clark's work on Euclidean quadratic forms, we introduce trace Euclidean and house Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields, and relate these concepts through the $p$-norm Euclidean property. We prove that, as $F$ varies over all totally real number fields of arbitrary degree, there are only finitely many positive definite trace Euclidean $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattices of arbitrary rank $n\ge1$, up to isometry. For every $p\in[1,\infty]$, the same finiteness holds for positive definite $p$-norm Euclidean lattices. We also classify all positive definite trace Euclidean lattices of rank one over real quadratic fields: there are exactly six isometry classes, and every such lattice is free. As a corollary, the trace Euclidean real quadratic fields are precisely $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$, $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{13})$.

papers.title: Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
papers.abstract: We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_δ(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2δ})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_δ(r_0+\varepsilon^δ)$, for every $0<δ<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.

papers.title: Dual near-factorizations and Schur products in association schemes
papers.abstract: Let $G$ and $H$ be Gram matrices of spherical $2$-designs on the same number of indices. We study when their Schur product is again the Gram matrix of a spherical design. We give a criterion in terms of orthogonal projections with constant diagonal, and an explicit $15$-point spherical $3$-design whose Gram matrix belongs to no symmetric Bose-Mesner algebra. For a symmetric association scheme, the factorization problem takes the form $v(E_S\circ E_T)=μE_U$. This is a counterpart of ordinary matrix product factorizations in the adjacency basis. The case $E_U=I-E_0$ gives a dual near-factorization and has a regular simplex as its normalized output. We characterize complementary input supports by a strongly regular fusion, give a reciprocal criterion, and classify the case in which one factor is the last Hamming idempotent.

papers.title: Homological and homotopical epimorphisms in monoidal $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We compare homological and homotopical epimorphisms of associative algebras in monoidal $\infty$-categories. Assume that geometric realizations and pushouts of associative algebras exist and that tensoring preserves geometric realizations. Then every homological epimorphism is homotopical. If, in addition, the ambient category is additive and tensoring preserves finite coproducts, the converse holds. This extends the result of Chuang and Lazarev for dg-algebras. In the symmetric monoidal setting, we discuss consequences for centers and commutative refinements, as well as applications to derived analytic geometry.

papers.title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
papers.abstract: A central limitation of modern machine learning systems is the lack of formal certificates guaranteeing their behavior beyond empirical, sample-based evaluation. Sum-of-squares (SOS) methods provide such guarantees by certifying polynomial inequalities over continuous domains via semidefinite programming (SDP). While prior work has introduced SDP layers as differentiable components in neural networks, repeated learning calls can lose the computational benefit of the forward program's sparse representation. We propose Sparse SOS Layers, differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the local coordinates of the forward solve. Under a fixed template and learned objective coefficients, each layer avoids building dense certificates and reuses its sparse structure across training steps. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves up to 2.7 times speedup in total warm-call time, with nearly 100 times lower memory usage (1.7 vs. 160 GiB) for relatively large problem sizes for the tested dense parameterization. Experiments cover sparse polynomial certification, pendulum control, combinatorial relaxations, robotics projection, oscillator chains, and pose graph synchronization. A design study achieves zero certified violations across unseen problem instances and sizes, while requiring roughly 7 times fewer optimization solves than estimating gradients by perturbing the objective coefficients and re-solving the problem (finite differences). These results show that sparse certificate values can be effectively integrated into learning pipelines when the backward pass respects the verifier's structure.

papers.title: Scattering for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and the Steklov spectrum
papers.abstract: We develop scattering theory for Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) maps on asymptotically conic, unbounded domains $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, that are only Lipschitz inside a compact set and whose boundary extends to infinity. Specifically, we prove a limiting absorption principle and demonstrate existence of the scattering matrix. As an application of the theory, we show that the eigenvalues of Steklov-type problems on curvilinear polygons, $\mathcal{P}$, are well approximated by the eigenvalues of a Dirac operator on $\partial\mathcal{P}$ whose transmission coefficients between edges meeting at a corner are given by the scattering matrix for DtN maps on asymptotically conic domains associated to the corners. Up to an arbitrary loss in the power of the eigenvalue, the error in the approximation is optimal among all possible asymptotics that use only local information about $\partial\mathcal{P}$.

papers.title: Independent powers and bounded Fourier partial sums in $L^1$
papers.abstract: We construct a probability measure on the circle with independent convolution powers and uniformly bounded symmetric Fourier partial sums in $L^1$. Every positive convolution power is therefore singular with respect to Haar measure. The measure is Rajchman. The construction answers a question of Andersson concerning measures with bounded Fourier partial sums outside the radical of $L^1$, and contrasts with his theorem that the classical examples of Weiss, Katznelson, and Brown-Hewitt have convolution squares in $L^2$. Our proof combines sparse probability blocks, an endpoint $L\log L$ estimate, and a diagonal generalized Riesz product. Exact factorization of local moments permits the simultaneous separation of all convolution powers by Brown's singularity criterion. By the classical spectral theory of independent-power measures, its spectrum is the closed unit disc. In particular, it has non-natural spectrum and induces a non-decomposable convolution operator on $L^1$. The image of the measure in $M(\mathbb T)/L^1(\mathbb T)$ has spectral radius one, and the closed unital algebra it generates in $M(\mathbb T)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^1(\mathbb N_0)$.

papers.title: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent
papers.abstract: A robot searching for the source of an odor must eventually answer a deceptively hard question: have I arrived? Near the source, concentration gradients flatten, turbulence makes the signal intermittent, and a small robot often lacks the positional accuracy to map the plume. Here, we describe a lightweight remedy inspired by a World War II statistics conundrum: the German tank problem. To approximate enemy armament production, Allied analysts developed an estimator based on serial numbers from captured tanks. Analogously, we use the same procedure over sampled chemical sensor readings from a robot to create estimates for the peak concentration of an odor plume, and therefore the odor's source. Treating each sensor reading as an observation, our unbiased estimator needs only a running maximum and a sample counter. An exact confidence bound turns both numbers into a principled rule that the robot or UAV can use to determine whether to keep searching for the plume source or land. We derive the estimator and its bound, demonstrate its sample efficiency, and examine its robustness even when its assumptions fail. Finally, we summarize the estimator's role as the termination criterion for olfactory navigation.

papers.title: Uniform observability criteria for linear time-varying systems
papers.abstract: Verifying uniform observability of a linear time-varying system generally requires its state-transition matrix. This paper develops necessary and sufficient conditions that can be checked directly from the coefficient matrices for two classes of systems. For constant dynamics with real spectrum and a measurable, essentially bounded output matrix, uniform observability is equivalent to persistent excitation of the output matrix on each eigenspace. An equivalent condition requires persistent excitation of the Kalman observability stack. The second result concerns cascades with a constant observable measured subsystem coupled to a hidden state. Under uniform regularity assumptions, linear combinations of output derivatives eliminate the measured state and yield an equivalent observability test for the hidden dynamics. When those dynamics have real spectrum, the test reduces to excitation on each eigenspace intersected with the kernel of the direct measurements. An application to arbitrary-order integrator chains with measurements of ranges to fixed anchors gives an exact excitation condition for the associated lifted LTV system. A second application treats direct hidden measurements and compares the condition with existing sufficient tests.

papers.title: Bounds for the univalent Bloch-Landau constant
papers.abstract: The univalent Bloch-Landau constant $\mathcal{U}$ is the largest number such that, for every univalent function $f$ on the unit disk, $f(\mathbb{D})$ contains a disk of radius $\mathcal{U} |f'(0)|$. We prove $0.612242\le\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$. The previous lower bound, $0.57088586$, came from growth estimates, which control disks centered at $f(0)$. Our improvement rests on a different mechanism. After Landau's normalization, a $2\times2$ compression of the Grunsky matrix constrains every omitted value through the same two coefficients, and choosing the center of the disk from these coefficients exploits this shared information. A short analytic proof based on this idea gives $\mathcal{U}\ge0.592$; it has been formalized in Lean, with the classical Grunsky and Fekete-Szegő inequalities as the only external inputs. Retaining complex quadratic forms of the matrix gives $\mathcal{U}\ge0.612242$ through a finite interval certificate, and this bound holds for every normalized univalent function with $a_2=0$ and $|a_3|\le1/3$. We also show that no argument based on disks centered at $f(0)$ can give a bound above $0.6$. For the upper bound we construct an explicit domain, bounded by Goodman's first two slit generations, thirty analytic arcs and a circle. We certify $\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$ with a capacity estimate for almost critical arcs, improving the best published bound $0.6563937$.

papers.title: A 1.932 Guarantee for (r,Q) Policies in Continuous-Review Lost-Sales Inventory Systems
papers.abstract: We provide a uniform guarantee for a continuous-review lost-sales inventory system with unit Poisson demand, deterministic lead time, and fixed ordering costs: a simple algorithm computes an $(r,Q)$ policy and chooses between that policy and no replenishment, with cost at most $(\sqrt2+\sqrt6)/2<1.932$ times the unrestricted nonanticipative optimum. The algorithm starts by generating an optimal integer base-stock policy, which at zero setup cost achieves the tight worst-case factor $\sqrt2$ relative to the optimal system cost. For positive setup costs, it uses the reorder point of this integer base-stock policy and an integer lot at the economic order quantity scale. The inclusion of ordinary base stock in the continuous-review capped base-stock family also improves that family's earlier asymptotic $1.79$ upper guarantee to a uniform $\sqrt2$ guarantee valid at every finite parameter vector. To establish these guarantees, we construct a computable lower bound on the zero-setup optimal cost by tracking units already on hand or committed for delivery. We then combine it with a bound on holding and setup costs required by batching to obtain the general-setup guarantee and instance-specific performance bounds for any admissible replenishment policy. In our numerical study, the largest estimated policy-cost-to-lower-bound ratios are about $1.59$ for our heuristic $(r, Q)$ policy and $1.47$ after joint optimization of $r$ and $Q$. The heuristic also performs well against the optimized policy: over the sampled instances, its median extra cost ranges from $2.33\%$ to $3.91\%$, depending on the setup cost.

papers.title: Chain flaring fails on the rose for atoroidal irreducible automorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that the chain flare condition introduced by Clay fails for every topological representative on the topological $n$-rose of every power of an atoroidal irreducible automorphism of $F_n$.

papers.title: Concentration of Exponential Tilts Implies Curvature
papers.abstract: We show, under a smoothness assumption, that probability measures whose exponential tilts have a uniformly bounded variance are given by a strongly convex potential, up to a bounded perturbation, yielding a partial converse to the Bakry-Émery theorem combined with Holley-Stroock's perturbation principle. A stronger version enforcing uniform convexity of the potential is obtained by considering the low-temperature regime.

papers.title: Correlation inequalities for volume polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish sharp correlation inequalities for volume polynomials associated with covers of multisets. These inequalities simultaneously generalize the Khovanskii--Teissier and reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities for intersections of nef divisor classes on projective varieties. They also hold for volume polynomials arising from convex bodies and Hermitian matrices, recovering and extending classical results such as the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequality for mixed volumes of convex bodies and the Hadamard--Fischer inequality for determinants of positive semidefinite matrices. As a combinatorial application, we prove a negative correlation inequality for partitions of bases of matroids that are linearly realizable over a field.

papers.title: Variational principle for the Carathéodory--Pesin entropy of foliations
papers.abstract: We introduce Carathéodory-Pesin structures for non-singular foliations on Riemannian manifolds and define a new notion of entropy for such foliations. Under dynamical and geometric assumptions on the corresponding holonomy pseudogroups, we establish a variational description of this new concept which relates it to the local metric entropy of measures on transversals and to the entropy of harmonic measures on the manifold.

papers.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{η_1,\ldots,η_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $η_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{η_i,η_j\in S:η_i\neqη_j}|\mathcal N(η_i-η_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

papers.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations
papers.abstract: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted Hölder estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.

papers.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $Γ_0$
papers.abstract: What does a recursive definition mean when the logic is grounded, so a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? Kripke's answer for the special case of truth was the least fixed point. This paper takes that answer as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) already writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term, paradoxes included. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, so that accessibility, the winning positions of a game, and grounded truth itself each come with their own induction principle. The rule is sound for the omega model and the system is consistent, both machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL. With the rule, IGA proves Goodstein's theorem outright, in a logic without implication at an undecided hypothesis, and the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, both with every step of the arithmetic a grounded derivation. It proves the Cantor normal forms well-founded, from which the well-foundedness of the standard $\varepsilon_0$ notation system in HOL follows, and it certifies the Veblen notation as an ordinal below every $\varphi(n,0)$. It defines Kripke truth for RGA's own language as one fixed point that agrees with the omega model exactly. Two equivalences locate what the classical world has and the grounded one does not. IGA proves the whole Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for that order, and bivalence of accessibility for an order is sound exactly when the order is well-founded; so $Γ_0$ lies at most one instance of excluded middle away, at the accessibility predicate of the notation, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in a primitive-recursive form of Kleene's $\mathcal O$ are interderivable over IGA.

papers.title: Demand Estimation with Unobserved Stockout Substitution: Exact Likelihood Maximization
papers.abstract: When a product is sold out, customers who prefer it may buy a substitute or leave without purchasing. Efficient demand estimation in this setting is challenging when inventory is observed only at replenishments, because the stockout times, and hence the products available to each customer, are unobserved. Estimating demand efficiently under stockout substitution has been a challenging problem since Anupindi et al. (1998), and it has become more pressing as the scale of such problem instances grows thanks to innovations in retailing such as unmanned stores. We provide a complete solution to this problem for the multinomial logit (MNL) model, the most widely used model of customer choice. Using a continuous-time representation of the purchase process developed in Zhou et al. (2026), we show that the exact likelihood and its gradient are one-dimensional integrals, no matter how many products, customers, or stockouts there are. Both can be evaluated at a cost linear in the numbers of products and periods. Our method estimates demand for 2,000 products from 2,000 selling periods in under ten minutes.

papers.title: Experimental Mathematics: Discovering The Half-Derivative from First Principles
papers.abstract: This expository paper grew out of two lectures in Miller's Math 409: The little Questions (Williams College, Fall 2026). We explore fractional derivatives by asking what a ``half-derivative'' might mean if applying it twice is to recover an ordinary derivative. Linearity and a natural guess for the half-derivative of a power function lead to a functional equation related to the classical factorial recurrence. Choosing the familiar Gamma-function extension gives the classical formula \[ \mathscr{D}^{1/2}(x^n) \ =\ \frac{Γ(n+1)}{Γ(n+\tfrac12)}x^{n-1/2}. \] We derive $Γ(n+1)=n!$, evaluate $Γ(1/2)=\sqrtπ$ using the Gaussian integral, and verify the half-derivative formula with an elementary integral. Along the way, we explore how the Gamma function generalizes factorials and binomial coefficients beyond their classical domains, encounter the double factorial, see why the usual product rule fails, and examine the half-derivative of $e^x$. We also explain why the original requirements do not determine a unique operator. The treatment emphasizes motivation, the benefits of experimentation through accessible calculations in test cases, rather than the general theory of fractional calculus.

papers.title: Results for distinct covering systems with a prime minimum modulus $q \ge 11$
papers.abstract: We prove that if the smallest modulus of a covering system is a prime $q \ge 11$, then the sum of the reciprocals of the moduli is at least $1+10^{-28}$. This improves on a previous more general bound of the first two authors in this particular case. We also show that it is impossible to construct a covering system using distinct multiples of $q$ as moduli. Finally, we show as a corollary that it is impossible to construct $10$ distinct covering systems with the property that no modulus is used in more than one of the covering systems.

papers.title: Energy stability of explicit--implicit--null time discretizations for nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients admitting a scalar energy potential. The explicit--implicit--null (EIN) method avoids severe time step restrictions of explicit time stepping and costly Newton--Raphson iterations required by a fully implicit treatment of the nonlinearity. Using orthogonal projection of the Kirchhoff transform, we prove nonlinear energy stability for first- to third-order EIN time stepping coupled with a wide range of spatial discretizations that admit self-adjoint positive semidefinite discrete operators. Under an upper bound for the diffusion coefficient on relevant stage segments, two IMEX coefficient conditions yield sufficient stabilization bounds without any time step restriction. The estimates dissipate the original convex energy and allow degenerate diffusion. We also extend the analysis to diffusion systems with a scalar energy potential in a fixed positive definite metric, and to consistent positive-weight quadrature discretizations. Applications include porous-medium flow, nonlinear heat transfer in plasma, and multicomponent diffusion.

papers.title: Convergence of Independence Metropolis-Hastings Algorithms in High Dimensions: Iteration Lengths, Cutoff Profiles, and Diagnostic Unreliability
papers.abstract: We characterize the high-dimensional convergence of the arithmetic mean from the independence Metropolis-Hastings algorithm initialized at its proposal. Convergence is measured in the worst-case expected absolute error over bounded functions. We prove necessary and sufficient conditions for the mean to converge in relation to the importance weight. We precisely describe the logarithmic cutoff profile of the sharp decay to convergence where the relative entropy between the target and proposal determines the required iteration length. These results make connections between the required iterations of independence Metropolis-Hastings and importance sampling. For concentrating Bayesian posteriors, we illustrate how the required iteration time can be estimated providing concrete guidance for simulations. We justify the logarithmic cutoff analysis by showing a standard cutoff phenomenon is absent and prove that popular convergence diagnostics based on simulation output can validate inaccurate simulations.

papers.title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
papers.abstract: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.

papers.title: On the frieze patterns by Conway and Coxeter
papers.abstract: The story of frieze patterns started in 1970s with a paper by Coxeter and two short papers by Conway and Coxeter, one listing questions and the other providing brief answers. During the first three decades it was followed by only a handful of papers observing some further properties of the same objects. Then Propp (2005) and Caldero and Chapoton (2006) established connections between frieze patterns and the recent theory of cluster algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky in early 2000s. Since then the theory of frieze patterns exploded with new results, and frieze patterns found a wide spectrum of connections in various domains of mathematics, including combinatorics, geometry, representation theory and integrable systems. The literature on frieze patterns grew vastly and continues to expand. In this note we give a brief overview of some of the directions emerging from the papers by Conway and Coxeter and single out core ideas which were later replayed in different contexts.

papers.title: Frangible prime gaps
papers.abstract: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erdős. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.7416, 2.7984]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.

papers.title: Lax Pair for the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation
papers.abstract: We prove that the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation on any compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary admits a Lax pair $(L,B)$, where $L$ is a self-adjoint finite-rank perturbation of the Laplace-Beltrami operator and $B$ is a skew-adjoint operator of finite rank, both depending analytically on the phase space variables. We study the spectrum of $L$ using the perturbative determinant which is known to determine its spectrum and to admit a product representation similar to that of the generating function in KdV. We use this to show that the dynamics of the integrals of motion constructed in \cite{BoitiManfrin2026,BHMP,campos} admits a Lax pair formulation with the same operator $L$ and to get a new proof of the involutivity of these integrals.

papers.title: Generators and Lefschetz properties of general hyperplane arrangement apolar algebras
papers.abstract: Hyperplane arrangements are rich combinatorial, topological, and geometric objects with numerous applications. Apolarity is a method of turning a homogeneous polynomial into a finite graded Gorenstein algebra. Invariants of the apolar algebra of the defining equation of a hyperplane arrangement are invariants of the arrangement itself. We investigate such invariants, including the Hilbert function, minimal generators of the apolar ideal, and Lefschetz properties. The main focus of the article is on combinatorially general arrangements of degree d in dimension n with d between n and 2n-2. In this range, we determine the Hilbert function and conjecture that the same formula is valid for larger values of d too. Minimal generators of the apolar ideal in the initial degree are in natural bijection to the lines of the arrangement. The initial degree characterizes arrangements that are combinatorially general. Finally, we prove that the apolar algebra has the Weak Lefschetz Property and precisely characterize the Weak Lefschetz elements.

papers.title: A graded version of the separator theorem for planar graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every planar graph on $n$ vertices has a vertex ordering $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n$ in which each prefix $\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}$ is joined to at most $C\sqrt{i}$ elements of $\{v_{i+1},\ldots,v_n\}$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. Consequently, every prefix can be separated from its complement by deleting $O\left(\sqrt{i}\right)$ vertices lying entirely in its complement.

papers.title: Symbolic Direct Construction of Augmented Systems for Levenberg-Marquardt Power Flow
papers.abstract: Levenberg-Marquardt power flow (LMPF) addresses ill-conditioned equations and provides least-squares stationary points for infeasible operating requests. Conventional implementations form damped normal equations, where J^T J introduces fill, squares the spectral condition number of the undamped part, and adds sparse-product cost. We propose an augmented LMPF formulation with a symbolic-permutation-based Jacobian operator that fills the augmented blocks directly. We prove that the matrix is symmetric quasi-definite for positive damping, enabling fixed-order, pivot-free QDLDL factorization. This property also motivates the solver choice: KLU value-only refactorization can reuse an unsuitable pivot order, forcing fresh full factorizations on difficult LMPF trajectories. We further introduce one-probe adaptive trust-region initialization for the radius and damping. Direct assembly is 7.5-11.9x faster than the fastest coordinate-list path and 18.0-58.8x faster than cached normal-equation sparse-product formation; QDLDL reduces numerical refactorization and triangular-solve time by up to 3.40x on identical matrices. Adaptive initialization solves flat-started RTE cases in 19-25 factorizations, 7.5-11.6x faster than reproduced three-step LM. On case2383wp, our 84-iteration run performs 84 factorizations and 168 resolves in 237 ms, versus published times of 200.780-441.72 s with fewer outer iterations, corresponding to speedups of 847-1860x. These results require complete factorization and resolve accounting and reveal initialization and legacy-parameter effects. DC-initialized NR exhibits fast quadratic convergence throughout every tested solvable loading range, motivating clearer, reproducible definitions of ill-conditioned power-flow benchmarks.

papers.title: Mixing zone dynamics for the Saffman-Taylor instability with viscosity jump
papers.abstract: We construct mixing solutions to the incompressible porous media equation for fully unstable Muskat initial data. The mixing zone expands linearly in time around an evolving central interface. Our approach combines the $h$-principle with the inversion of the associated Birkhoff-Rott operator, required when the viscosities differ. A key ingredient is to formulate this inversion in terms of the Saffman-Taylor function rather than the vorticity. This considerably simplifies the analysis and may be of independent interest for the Muskat problem.

papers.title: Regularity of the solution map for the Oldroyd--B model with fractional stress dissipation
papers.abstract: The data-to-solution map of the incompressible Euler equations is continuous but not uniformly continuous on Sobolev spaces, whereas viscosity makes the Navier--Stokes solution map Lipschitz continuous on small data, uniformly in time. This paper identifies the behavior of the solution map for a hybrid system sitting between these two extremes: the incompressible Oldroyd--B model in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d=2,3$, in the high-Reynolds-number, high-Weissenberg-number regime. The velocity equation is a forced Euler equation and the only dissipation is a fractional diffusion $η(-Δ)^β$, $\frac12\leβ\le1$, acting on stress. We prove that, on the ball of small $H^s$ data ($s>1+\frac d2$) on which global solutions exist, the solution map is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the $H^{r}$-norm, $r=s-(2β-1)$, uniformly for all time, and Lipschitz into the natural dissipation spaces; the constant is explicit and tends to $\sqrt3$ as the size of the data tends to zero. Consequently the map is Hölder continuous into $C_b([0,\infty);H^{s'})$ for every $s'<s$, and is Lipschitz in $H^s$ itself when $β=\frac12$. Thus, although the velocity field is only transported, the solution map behaves like that of the Navier--Stokes equations rather than that of the Euler equations. The proof exploits the damped wave structure generated by the coupling between $u$ and $\nabla\cdotτ$ through a Lyapunov functional with a cross term $(δu,\nabla\cdotδτ)_{H^{r-β}}$, which transfers the stress dissipation to the velocity difference, together with a low-frequency interpolation argument that keeps all Gronwall coefficients integrable on $(0,\infty)$. The loss of $2β-1$ derivatives is exactly the gap between the hidden velocity dissipation of order $2(1-β)$ and the dissipation required by the Lipschitz estimate, and we show that it cannot be reduced by the energy method.

papers.title: Second-Order Steps, Spectral Accuracy: Discrete Parallel Transport of Invariant Subspaces
papers.abstract: Eigensolvers return orthonormal bases of invariant subspaces, but each basis is determined only up to a unitary factor, so bases computed at different parameter values cannot, in general, be interpolated directly. Discrete parallel transport resolves this ambiguity by aligning consecutive bases through the polar factors of their overlaps, but approximates the continuous parallel-transported frame only to second order. We show that the resulting frames can nevertheless be interpolated with spectral accuracy. For analytic families of invariant subspaces sampled at $N+1$ Chebyshev nodes, the computed frames are exact samples of an analytic frame related to the parallel-transported frame by a gauge that remains within $O(N^{-2})$ of the identity throughout a fixed complex neighborhood, uniformly in $N$. Consequently, Chebyshev interpolation approximates this analytic frame with geometric convergence. Moreover, the continuous parallel-transported frame can be recovered to spectral accuracy by solving a small matrix differential equation, without additional eigensolves or derivatives of the underlying matrix family. The results do not require the family to be Hermitian and remain valid through eigenvalue crossings and branch points, provided the selected invariant subspace depends analytically on the parameter. Numerical examples confirm the predicted rates.

papers.title: Certifying Distributionally Robust Decisions from Projection Observations
papers.abstract: A scalar measurement can determine a robust decision without identifying the latent covariance or every decision risk. We study finite Gaussian projection experiments with a fixed mean-plus-standard-deviation target. The observation laws define a set of indistinguishable moment models. We exhibit decisions that agree throughout that set despite unidentified risk values, and give a confidence-set certificate that returns a decision or an unresolved outcome. We prove soundness, necessary abstention for indistinguishable models with incompatible optima, and a fixed-checkpoint certification guarantee. A scalar profile reduces nonlinear risk comparisons to convex inner problems. Across seven synthetic instances, jointly calibrated moment regions give sufficient budgets 21 to 52 times explicit expected-sample information lower bounds. Separately measured stopping times are lower, with zero decision errors in 1,900 simulated streams. These comparisons do not constitute matching bounds, and the guarantees require Gaussian replication.

papers.title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
papers.abstract: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine.
